command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
[[ -f "$CONFIG" ]] || exit 0

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh

        | jq -r '[.checkpoint.task?, .checkpoint.sprint?, .sprint?] | map(select(type == "string" and . != ""))

    rm -f -- "$LEGACY" 2>/dev/null || true
    if [[ "$STATE_DIR" == "$DEFAULT_STATE_DIR" ]]; then
        rm -f -- "$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-state.v1.agg" \
                 "$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-config.v1.tokens" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
fi

# --- append to the task's file ------------------------------------------------
[[ -L "$STATE_DIR" ]] && exit 0
[[ -d "$STATE_DIR" ]] || mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
TASK_FILE="$STATE_DIR/$KEY.jsonl"
[[ -L "$TASK_FILE" ]] && exit 0

PRIOR=0
if [[ -f "$TASK_FILE" ]]; then
    # Tolerant of malformed lines: sums every `"lines_changed":<int>` it finds.
    PRIOR="$(awk -F'"lines_changed":' '/"lines_changed":/ { sum += $2 + 0 } END { print sum + 0 }' "$TASK_FILE" 2>/dev/null)" || PRIOR=0
    [[ "$PRIOR" =~ ^[0-9]{1,15}$ ]] || PRIOR=0
fi
RUNNING=$((PRIOR + LINES))

printf '{"ts":"%s","tool":"%s","file":%s,"lines_changed":%s,"running_total":%s,"session_id":%s,"task":"%s"}\n' \
    "$TS" "$TOOL_NAME" "$FILE_JSON" "$LINES" "$RUNNING" "$SESSION_JSON" "$KEY" >> "$TASK_FILE" 2>/dev/null || exit 0

# whitespace, no leading dot, so the glob and the ls listing are exact).
n=0
while IFS= read -r old; do
    n=$((n + 1))
    if (( n > KEEP )) && [[ "$old" != "$TASK_FILE" && ! -L "$old" ]]; then
        rm -f -- "$old" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
done < <(ls -1t -- "$STATE_DIR"/*.jsonl 2>/dev/null)

# --- summary (atomic) ---------------------------------------------------------
OVER=false
(( RUNNING > THRESHOLD )) && OVER=true
sum_dir="${SUMMARY%/*}"
[[ "$sum_dir" == "$SUMMARY" ]] && sum_dir="."
if [[ -d "$sum_dir" ]] || mkdir -p "$sum_dir" 2>/dev/null; then
    tmp="$SUMMARY.tmp.$$"
    if printf '{"task":"%s","lines":%s,"threshold":%s,"over":%s,"updated_at":"%s"}\n' \
            "$KEY" "$RUNNING" "$THRESHOLD" "$OVER" "$TS" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
        mv -f -- "$tmp" "$SUMMARY" 2>/dev/null || rm -f -- "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
    else

    fi

        ($s | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))) as $l |
        (try ([$l[] | fromjson | .file // empty] | unique | length) catch 0) as $f |
        "\($f) \($l | length)"' 2>/dev/null)" || counts="0 0"

    [[ "$FILES_MOD" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || FILES_MOD=0
    [[ "$TOOL_CALLS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || TOOL_CALLS=0
    [[ -d "$TRAJ_DIR" ]] || mkdir -p "$TRAJ_DIR" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
    printf '{"phase":"karpathy_check","principle":"surgical_changes","timestamp":"%s","files_modified":%s,"lines_total":%s,"threshold":%s,"verdict":"warn","tool_call_count":%s,"session_id":%s}\n' \
        "$TS" "$FILES_MOD" "$RUNNING" "$THRESHOLD" "$TOOL_CALLS" "$SESSION_JSON" \
        >> "$TRAJ_DIR/karpathy-${TS:0:10}.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

exit 0

tool_use_result.stdout:
fi
 fi

SESSION="${payload_sid:-${LOA_SESSION_ID:-}}"
[[ -n "$SESSION" ]] || SESSION="${USER:-unknown}-${TS:0:4}${TS:5:2}${TS:8:2}"
SESSION_JSON="$(jq -cn --arg s "$SESSION" '$s')"

task_raw=""
if [[ -f "$CHECKPOINT" ]]; then
    task_raw="$(bash "$CHECKPOINT" read --json 2>/dev/null \
        | jq -r '[.checkpoint.task?, .checkpoint.sprint?, .sprint?] | map(select(type == "string" and . != ""))
                  | .[0] // empty | gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9._-]"; "_")' 2>/dev/null \
        | head -1)" || task_raw=""
fi
KEY="$(_sanitise "$task_raw")"
[[ -n "$KEY" ]] || KEY="$(_sanitise "$SESSION")"
[[ -n "$KEY" ]] || KEY="session-unknown"

# --- legacy layout: deleted on the first run under this one -------------------
if [[ -e "$LEGACY" || -L "$LEGACY" ]]; then
    rm -f -- "$LEGACY" 2>/dev/null || true
    if [[ "$STATE_DIR" == "$DEFAULT_STATE_DIR" ]]; then
        rm -f -- "$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-state.v1.agg" \
                 "$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-config.v1.tokens" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
fi

# --- append to the task's file ------------------------------------------------
[[ -L "$STATE_DIR" ]] && exit 0
[[ -d "$STATE_DIR" ]] || mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
TASK_FILE="$STATE_DIR/$KEY.jsonl"
[[ -L "$TASK_FILE" ]] && exit 0

PRIOR=0
if [[ -f "$TASK_FILE" ]]; then
    # Tolerant of malformed lines: sums every `"lines_changed":<int>` it finds.
    PRIOR="$(awk -F'"lines_changed":' '/"lines_changed":/ { sum += $2 + 0 } END { print sum + 0 }' "$TASK_FILE" 2>/dev/null)" || PRIOR=0
    [[ "$PRIOR" =~ ^[0-9]{1,15}$ ]] || PRIOR=0
fi
RUNNING=$((PRIOR + LINES))

printf '{"ts":"%s","tool":"%s","file":%s,"lines_changed":%s,"running_total":%s,"session_id":%s,"task":"%s"}\n' \
    "$TS" "$TOOL_NAME" "$FILE_JSON" "$LINES" "$RUNNING" "$SESSION_JSON" "$KEY" >> "$TASK_FILE" 2>/dev/null || exit 0

# Keep the KEEP most recently written task files (names are sanitised: no
# whitespace, no leading dot, so the glob and the ls listing are exact).
n=0
while IFS= read -r old; do
    n=$((n + 1))
    if (( n > KEEP )) && [[ "$old" != "$TASK_FILE" && ! -L "$old" ]]; then
        rm -f -- "$old" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
done < <(ls -1t -- "$STATE_DIR"/*.jsonl 2>/dev/null)

# --- summary (atomic) ---------------------------------------------------------
OVER=false
(( RUNNING > THRESHOLD )) && OVER=true
sum_dir="${SUMMARY%/*}"
[[ "$sum_dir" == "$SUMMARY" ]] && sum_dir="."
if [[ -d "$sum_dir" ]] || mkdir -p "$sum_dir" 2>/dev/null; then
    tmp="$SUMMARY.tmp.$$"
    if printf '{"task":"%s","lines":%s,"threshold":%s,"over":%s,"updated_at":"%s"}\n' \
            "$KEY" "$RUNNING" "$THRESHOLD" "$OVER" "$TS" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
        mv -f -- "$tmp" "$SUMMARY" 2>/dev/null || rm -f -- "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
    else
        rm -f -- "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
    fi
fi

# --- warning + trajectory event -----------------------------------------------
if [[ "$OVER" == "true" ]]; then
    echo "[karpathy-surgical-warn] Session diff total ${RUNNING} lines exceeds threshold ${THRESHOLD}. Karpathy principle 3 (Surgical Changes): verify every changed line traces to the stated task. State: $TASK_FILE" >&2

    counts="$(jq -nr --rawfile s "$TASK_FILE" '
        ($s | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))) as $l |
        (try ([$l[] | fromjson | .file // empty] | unique | length) catch 0) as $f |
        "\($f) \($l | length)"' 2>/dev/null)" || counts="0 0"
    FILES_MOD="${counts%% *}"; TOOL_CALLS="${counts##* }"
    [[ "$FILES_MOD" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || FILES_MOD=0
    [[ "$TOOL_CALLS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || TOOL_CALLS=0
    [[ -d "$TRAJ_DIR" ]] || mkdir -p "$TRAJ_DIR" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
    printf '{"phase":"karpathy_check","principle":"surgical_changes","timestamp":"%s","files_modified":%s,"lines_total":%s,"threshold":%s,"verdict":"warn","tool_call_count":%s,"session_id":%s}\n' \
        "$TS" "$FILES_MOD" "$RUNNING" "$THRESHOLD" "$TOOL_CALLS" "$SESSION_JSON" \
        >> "$TRAJ_DIR/karpathy-${TS:0:10}.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

exit 0

index f9aa8c41..28684653 100755
--- a/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh
+++ b/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh
@@ -120,6 +120,649 @@
 # is exec'd only inside emit_block and the FR-SZ bypass audit branch).
 # =============================================================================
 
+# =============================================================================
+# FR-6 heredoc consumer classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1; knob
+# destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier, default true; false = the
+# pre-cycle scan, i.e. only the #1245 quoted-cat scrub below).
+# Defined BEFORE the bash-version guard and the stdin read so another script
+# can source this file with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 and call
+#   _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   → prints interpreter|nonexec|none
+#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>               → exit 0 iff nonexec
+# Bash 3.2 compatible (no ${x,,}, no mapfile, no associative arrays) and safe
+# under a caller's `set -u`.
+#
+# Grammar (literal command text; no alias or function expansion; CRLF folded
+# to LF). The command is walked line by line; a line holding an unquoted
+# `<<` / `<<-` (not `<<<`) is a heredoc header, the body runs to the first
+# line equal to the delimiter (leading tabs stripped for `<<-`). FULL SCAN
+# (the whole command as today) on: any other control character, a header the
+# tokenizer cannot read (open quote, trailing backslash, comment), more than
+# one heredoc on a header, a delimiter that is not a plain word ('W', "W",
+# \W or W with W in [A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]; `$X` is a variable delimiter), or a
+# missing terminator. Per heredoc the class is:
+#   interpreter — body scanned exactly as today: the header holds `$(`, a
+#     backtick, `<(` or `>(`, a paren or brace group or a shell keyword; it
+#     continues on the next line (`|`, `&&`, `||` last) or an earlier line
+#     opened a substitution, group, quote or pipe; a member of the heredoc's
+#     pipeline is a shell, interpreter, wrapper that runs its argument or SQL
+#     runner (_bdb_hd_is_interp, _bdb_hd_is_runner); an allowlisted form
+#     carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag (-c, -e, -x clusters, --exec,
+#     --eval, --command, in-place); a write target is executable content
+#     (_bdb_hd_exec_dest: script extension, .claude/hooks, .claude/settings*
+#     .json, .git/hooks, .git/config, rc/profile files, /etc, a bin dir or a
+#     directory on PATH, or any non-literal path); the first body line is a
+#     shebang; the body holds `<<` (nested); a target's basename appears
+#     elsewhere in the command outside the safe readers (_bdb_hd_same_line_exec:
+#     `bash x`, `./x`, `source x`, `. x`, `chmod +x x`, `exec x`, cp/mv …).
+#   nonexec — every pipeline member is an exact allowlisted form
+#     (_bdb_hd_member): cat, tee, printf, echo with plain-file or stdout sinks;
+#     gh pr|issue comment -F -; gh pr create --body-file -; git commit -F -;
+#     br create|update reading `-`; jq/yq without in-place; grep; sed -n with
+#     a print-only script; sort; wc. The body is then scanned PER SEGMENT
+#     (_bdb_hd_scan_body): each line split on ; && || | &, wrapper prefixes
+#     stripped (sudo command exec env nice time nohup builtin stdbuf ionice,
+#     a leading backslash, quote, paren or brace, assignments, an absolute
+#     path); a segment whose command word is a fence verb (rm git find dd
+#     mkfs* shred truncate kubectl terraform aws gcloud psql mysql DROP
+#     DELETE TRUNCATE) is kept on its own line for the normal rules, other
+#     segments are dropped. The body falls back to a full scan when it holds
+#     `$(`, a backtick, `<(` or `>(` under an unquoted delimiter, or a segment
+#     word is an interpreter or wrapper, or a variable (`$x -rf /`; such a
+#     segment is ALSO scanned as rm, git and kubectl with the same arguments).
+#     Special case (the #1245 scrub): a standalone quoted-delimiter `cat`
+#     whose header is exactly `cat <<'W' [> path]` drops the whole body.

+_bdb_hd_op_re='^[0-9]*(<<<|<<-|&>>|<<|>>|>[|]|&&|[|][|]|[|]&|&>|<>|>&[0-9-]*|<&[0-9-]*|;;|;|&|[|]|<|>|[(]|[)])$'
+_bdb_hd_re_dw='^[A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+$'
+_bdb_hd_re_dsq="^'([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)'\$"
+_bdb_hd_re_ddq='^"([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)"$'
+_bdb_hd_re_dbs='^\\([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)$'
+_bdb_hd_re_psq="^'([^']*)'\$"
+_bdb_hd_re_pdq="^\"([^\"\$\`\\\\]*)\"\$"
+_bdb_hd_re_pbare="^[^'\"\$\`\\\\]+\$"

+_bdb_hd_re_exflag='^-[A-Za-z]*[cex][A-Za-z]*$'
+_bdb_hd_re_exlong='^--(exec|eval|command|in-?place)'

+_bdb_hd_is_interp() {
+  case "$1" in
+    bash|sh|zsh|dash|ksh|mksh|ash|fish|csh|tcsh|busybox|python|python[0-9]*|pypy*|node|nodejs|deno|bun|ruby|irb|perl|php|lua|luajit|tclsh|wish|expect|pwsh|powershell|osascript|Rscript) return 0 ;;

+_bdb_hd_is_runner() {
+  case "$1" in
+    psql|pgcli|mysql|mariadb|mysqlsh|sqlite3|sqlcmd|sqlplus|isql|usql|litecli|duckdb|clickhouse|clickhouse-client|cockroach|bq|wrangler|prisma|supabase|drizzle-kit|knex|sequelize|typeorm|flyway|liquibase|dbmate|goose|sqitch|rails|manage.py|artisan|alembic|dbt|atlas|mongosh|sqlx) return 0 ;;

+  return 1

+    rm|git|find|dd|shred|truncate|kubectl|terraform|aws|gcloud|psql|mysql|mkfs|mkfs.*) return 0 ;;

+  return 1

+    cat|ls|wc|head|tail|grep|egrep|fgrep|rg|diff|cmp|stat|file|test|'['|echo|printf|sort|uniq|jq|yq|git|gh|br|mkdir|touch|realpath|readlink|basename|dirname|du|md5sum|sha1sum|sha256sum|shasum|b2sum|cksum) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  return 1

+# _bdb_hd_tokenize <line> → _bdb_hd_tok[] (words keep their quotes; operators
+# are separate tokens, an fd number joins its redirect). Returns 1 when the
+# line cannot be read: open quote, trailing backslash, unquoted comment.
+_bdb_hd_tokenize() {
+  local s="${1:-}" n i=0 ch tok="" q="" have=0 op cand
+  n=${#s}
+  _bdb_hd_tok=()
+  while (( i < n )); do
+    ch="${s:i:1}"
+    if [[ -n "$q" ]]; then
+      tok="$tok$ch"
+      if [[ "$q" == "'" ]]; then
+        [[ "$ch" == "'" ]] && q=""
+      elif [[ "$ch" == '\' ]]; then
+        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
+        i=$((i + 1)); tok="$tok${s:i:1}"
+      elif [[ "$ch" == '"' ]]; then
+        q=""
+      fi
+      i=$((i + 1)); continue
+    fi
+    case "$ch" in
+      "'"|'"') q="$ch"; tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+      '\')
+        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
+        tok="$tok$ch${s:i+1:1}"; have=1; i=$((i + 2)) ;;
+      ' '|$'\t')
+        if (( have )); then _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"; tok=""; have=0; fi
+        i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+      '#')
+        (( have )) || return 1
+        tok="$tok$ch"; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+      ';'|'&'|'|'|'<'|'>'|'('|')')
+        op=""
+        for cand in '<<<' '<<-' '&>>' '<<' '>>' '>|' '&&' '||' '|&' '&>' '<>' '>&' '<&' ';;' ';' '&' '|' '<' '>' '(' ')'; do
+          if [[ "${s:i:${#cand}}" == "$cand" ]]; then op="$cand"; break; fi
+        done
+        i=$((i + ${#op}))
+        if [[ "$op" == '>&' || "$op" == '<&' ]]; then
+          while (( i < n )) && [[ "${s:i:1}" == [0-9-] ]]; do op="$op${s:i:1}"; i=$((i + 1)); done
+        fi
+        if (( have )); then
+          if [[ "$tok" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$op" == '<'* || "$op" == '>'* ]]; then
+            op="$tok$op"
+          else
+            _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
+          fi
+          tok=""; have=0
+        fi
+        _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$op" ;;
+      *) tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+    esac
+  done
+  [[ -z "$q" ]] || return 1
+  (( have )) && _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
+  return 0
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_unq_path <word> → _hd_up; returns 1 for a non-literal path (an
+# expansion, an escape, mixed quoting) or an empty one.
+_bdb_hd_unq_path() {
+  _hd_up=""
+  if [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_psq ]] || [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pdq ]]; then
+    _hd_up="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
+  elif [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pbare ]]; then
+    _hd_up="$1"
+  else
+    return 1
+  fi
+  [[ -n "$_hd_up" ]]
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_exec_dest <unquoted path> → 0 when a write there is executable
+# content (or cannot be judged).
+_bdb_hd_exec_dest() {
+  local p="${1:-}" d e b old_ifs
+  case "$p" in
+    *'*'*|*'?'*|*'['*|*'{'*|'~'|'~'[!/]*|'') return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  [[ "$p" == '~/'* ]] && p="${HOME:-}/${p#'~/'}"
+  b="${p##*/}"
+  [[ "$b" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ext ]] && return 0
+  [[ "$p" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_sys || "$p" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_rc ]] && return 0
+  [[ "$p" == /etc/* ]] && return 0
+  if [[ "$p" == /* ]]; then d="${p%/*}"; [[ -n "$d" ]] || d="/"
+  elif [[ "$p" == */* ]]; then d="${PWD:-.}/${p%/*}"
+  else d="${PWD:-.}"
+  fi
+  old_ifs="$IFS"; IFS=':'
+  for e in ${PATH:-}; do
+    [[ -z "$e" || "$e" == "." ]] && e="${PWD:-.}"
+    [[ "$e" != "/" ]] && e="${e%/}"
+    if [[ "$d" == "$e" ]]; then IFS="$old_ifs"; return 0; fi
+  done
+  IFS="$old_ifs"
+  return 1
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_member <tokens…> → _hd_mcls (interpreter|nonexec|none) for one
+# pipeline member; write targets are appended to _hd_dests.
+_bdb_hd_member() {
+  local -a toks argv
+  local t nxt i n stdout_files=0 a0 base fd stdin=0 ops=0 want="" has_n=0 script=""
+  toks=("$@"); n=${#toks[@]}; argv=()

+  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
+    t="${toks[i]}"
+    if [[ "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_op_re ]]; then
+      case "$t" in
+        *'<<<') return ;;
+        *'<<'|*'<<-') i=$((i + 1)); continue ;;
+        *'>&'[0-9]*|*'>&-'|*'<&'*) continue ;;
+        *'>'|*'>>'|*'>|'|*'>&'|'&>'|'&>>')
+          nxt="${toks[i+1]:-}"; i=$((i + 1))
+          if [[ -z "$nxt" || "$nxt" =~ $_bdb_hd_op_re ]]; then _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; fi
+          _bdb_hd_unq_path "$nxt" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }

+          _hd_dests[${#_hd_dests[@]}]="$_hd_up"
+          fd="${t%%[>&]*}"
+          [[ -z "$fd" || "$fd" == 1 || "$t" == '&>'* || "$t" == '>&' ]] && stdout_files=$((stdout_files + 1))
+          continue ;;
+        *) return ;;
+      esac
+    fi
+    argv[${#argv[@]}]="$t"
+  done

+  (( ${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]} > 0 )) || return 1
+  last="${_bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}-1]}"
+  case "$last" in '|'|'|&'|'&&'|'||') return 0 ;; esac
+  return 1
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_header <line> — parse one header line. Sets _hd_ops (heredoc count,
+# -1 = unreadable), _hd_delim, _hd_quoted, _hd_tabs, _hd_cls, _hd_dests[],
+# _hd_pipe (pipeline id of the heredoc on this line).
+_bdb_hd_header() {
+  local line="${1:-}" k nt t opi=-1 w seg=0 pipe=0
+  local -a tpipe mtoks
+  _hd_ops=0 _hd_delim="" _hd_quoted=0 _hd_tabs=0 _hd_cls=none _hd_pipe=-1
+  _hd_dests=()
+  if ! _bdb_hd_tokenize "$line"; then _hd_ops=-1; return; fi
+  nt=${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}
+  tpipe=()
+  for ((k = 0; k < nt; k++)); do
+    t="${_bdb_hd_tok[k]}"
+    case "$t" in
+      ';'|';;'|'&'|'&&'|'||'|'('|')') pipe=$((pipe + 1)); tpipe[k]=-1; continue ;;
+      '|'|'|&') tpipe[k]=-1; continue ;;
+    esac
+    tpipe[k]=$pipe
+    if [[ "$t" =~ ^[0-9]*'<<'-?$ ]]; then _hd_ops=$((_hd_ops + 1)); opi=$k; fi
+  done
+  (( _hd_ops == 1 )) || return
+  w="${_bdb_hd_tok[opi+1]:-}"
+  [[ "${_bdb_hd_tok[opi]}" == *'<<-' ]] && _hd_tabs=1
+  if [[ "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_dsq || "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ddq || "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_dbs ]]; then
+    _hd_delim="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"; _hd_quoted=1
+  elif [[ "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_dw ]]; then
+    _hd_delim="$w"
+  else
+    _hd_ops=-1; return        # variable-expanded, mixed or missing delimiter
+  fi
+  _hd_pipe="${tpipe[opi]}"
+  if _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$line"; then _hd_cls=interpreter; return; fi
+  _bdb_hd_tokenize "$line"    # _bdb_hd_ctx_bad reused the token buffer
+  # Classify every member of the heredoc's pipeline; the most executing wins.
+  local cls=nonexec
+  k=0
+  while (( k < nt )); do
+    if [[ "${tpipe[k]}" != "$_hd_pipe" ]]; then k=$((k + 1)); continue; fi
+    mtoks=()
+    while (( k < nt )) && [[ "${tpipe[k]}" == "$_hd_pipe" ]]; do mtoks[${#mtoks[@]}]="${_bdb_hd_tok[k]}"; k=$((k + 1)); done
+    _bdb_hd_member "${mtoks[@]}"
+    case "$_hd_mcls" in
+      interpreter) cls=interpreter ;;
+      none) [[ "$cls" == interpreter ]] || cls=none ;;
+    esac
+    k=$((k + 1))
+  done
+  _hd_cls="$cls"
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_segword <segment> → _hd_w (command word after wrapper stripping,
+# quotes and an absolute path removed) and _hd_rest (the text after it).
+_bdb_hd_segword() {
+  local s="${1:-}" w guard=0
+  _hd_w="" _hd_rest=""
+  while (( guard < 64 )); do
+    guard=$((guard + 1))
+    s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
+    [[ -n "$s" ]] || return
+    case "${s:0:1}" in
+      '('|'{'|'!'|'\'|'"'|"'") s="${s:1}"; continue ;;
+    esac
+    w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"
+    s="${s:${#w}}"
+    if [[ "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_assign ]]; then continue; fi
+    case "$w" in
+      sudo|doas|command|exec|env|nice|time|nohup|builtin|stdbuf|ionice)
+        while :; do
+          s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
+          case "$s" in
+            -S|-S[[:space:]]*|--split-string*) _hd_w="sh"; _hd_rest="$s"; return ;;
+            -[ugnCphUrtTDc]|-[ugnCphUrtTDc][[:space:]]*)
+              s="${s:2}"; s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"; s="${s:${#w}}" ;;
+            -*) w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"; s="${s:${#w}}" ;;
+            *) break ;;
+          esac
+        done
+        continue ;;
+    esac
+    w="${w%%[\"\']*}"
+    [[ "$w" == */* && "$w" != '$'* ]] && w="${w##*/}"
+    _hd_w="$w"; _hd_rest="$s"
+    return
+  done
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_scan_body <first> <last> <quoted> — per-segment scan of
+# _bdb_hd_L[first..last]. Sets _hd_kept (fence-verb segments, one per line),
+# _hd_synth (variable-command segments rewritten as rm/git/kubectl) and
+# _hd_full (1 = the body needs the full scan).
+_bdb_hd_scan_body() {
+  local k l t seg
+  _hd_kept="" _hd_synth="" _hd_full=0
+  for ((k = $1; k <= $2; k++)); do
+    l="${_bdb_hd_L[k]}"
+    [[ "$l" == *'<<'* ]] && _hd_full=1
+    if (( ! $3 )); then
+      case "$l" in *'$('*|*'`'*|*'<('*|*'>('*) _hd_full=1 ;; esac
+    fi
+    t="${l//'&&'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//'||'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//'|'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//';'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//'&'/$'\n'}"
+    while :; do
+      seg="${t%%$'\n'*}"
+      _bdb_hd_segword "$seg"
+      if [[ -n "$_hd_w" ]]; then
+        if [[ "$_hd_w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_varw ]]; then
+          _hd_full=1
+          _hd_synth="${_hd_synth}rm${_hd_rest}"$'\n'"git${_hd_rest}"$'\n'"kubectl${_hd_rest}"$'\n'
+        elif _bdb_hd_is_destructive "$_hd_w"; then
+          _hd_kept="${_hd_kept}${_hd_w}${_hd_rest}"$'\n'
+        elif _bdb_hd_is_interp "$_hd_w" || _bdb_hd_is_runner "$_hd_w"; then
+          _hd_full=1
+        fi
+      fi
+      [[ "$t" == *$'\n'* ]] || break
+      t="${t#*$'\n'}"
+    done
+  done
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_same_line_exec <basename> <header idx> <body first> <body last>
+# → 0 when the target is named anywhere else in the command outside a safe
+# reader (it may be executed, sourced, made executable, copied or moved).
+_bdb_hd_same_line_exec() {
+  local b="$1" hi="$2" bf="$3" bl="$4" k nt t u c cw seg_has pipe start j own
+  for ((k = 0; k < _bdb_hd_n; k++)); do
+    (( k >= bf && k <= bl )) && continue
+    [[ "${_bdb_hd_L[k]}" == *"$b"* ]] || continue
+    _bdb_hd_tokenize "${_bdb_hd_L[k]}" || return 0
+    nt=${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}
+    start=0 pipe=0
+    for ((j = 0; j <= nt; j++)); do
+      t="${_bdb_hd_tok[j]:-}"
+      if (( j < nt )) && ! [[ "$t" =~ ^(';'|';;'|'&'|'&&'|'||'|'('|')'|'|'|'|&')$ ]]; then continue; fi
+      # segment [start, j)
+      own=0
+      (( k == hi && pipe == _hd_pipe_saved )) && own=1
+      if (( ! own )); then
+        seg_has=0 cw=""
+        for ((c = start; c < j; c++)); do
+          u="${_bdb_hd_tok[c]}"; u="${u//[\"\']/}"; u="${u##*/}"
+          [[ "$u" == "$b" ]] && seg_has=1
+        done
+        if (( seg_has )); then
+          _bdb_hd_segword "${_bdb_hd_tok[*]:start:j-start}"
+          cw="$_hd_w"
+          if ! _bdb_hd_is_safe_reader "$cw" || [[ "$cw" == "$b" ]]; then return 0; fi
+        fi
+      fi
+      case "$t" in '|'|'|&') ;; *) pipe=$((pipe + 1)) ;; esac
+      start=$((j + 1))
+    done
+  done
+  return 1
+}
+
+# _bdb_heredoc_scrub <command> — print the scrub copy (non-executing heredoc
+# bodies reduced to their fence-verb segments) and set _bdb_hd_class to the
+# most executing class seen (interpreter > none > nonexec; none if no heredoc).
+_bdb_heredoc_scrub() {
+  local text="${1:-}" out="" i j found l cls ctx=0 seen="" d first
+  _bdb_hd_class=none
+  text="${text//$'\r\n'/$'\n'}"
+  if [[ "$text" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ctl ]]; then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
+  text="${text%$'\n'}"
+  _bdb_hd_L=()
+  while IFS= read -r l; do _bdb_hd_L[${#_bdb_hd_L[@]}]="$l"; done <<< "$text"
+  _bdb_hd_n=${#_bdb_hd_L[@]}
+  i=0
+  while (( i < _bdb_hd_n )); do
+    l="${_bdb_hd_L[i]}"
+    if [[ "$l" != *'<<'* ]]; then
+      out="$out$l"$'\n'
+      (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
+      i=$((i + 1)); continue
+    fi
+    _bdb_hd_header "$l"
+    if (( _hd_ops == 0 )); then
+      out="$out$l"$'\n'
+      (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
+      i=$((i + 1)); continue
+    fi
+    if (( _hd_ops != 1 )); then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
+    found=-1
+    for ((j = i + 1; j < _bdb_hd_n; j++)); do
+      d="${_bdb_hd_L[j]}"
+      if (( _hd_tabs )); then while [[ "$d" == $'\t'* ]]; do d="${d#$'\t'}"; done; fi
+      if [[ "$d" == "$_hd_delim" ]]; then found=$j; break; fi
+    done
+    if (( found < 0 )); then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
+    cls="$_hd_cls"
+    (( ctx )) && cls=interpreter
+    _hd_pipe_saved="$_hd_pipe"
+    if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]]; then
+      first="${_bdb_hd_L[i+1]:-}"
+      (( i + 1 < found )) || first=""
+      first="${first#"${first%%[![:blank:]]*}"}"
+      [[ "$first" == '#!'* ]] && cls=interpreter
+    fi
+    if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]]; then
+      local -a dests
+      dests=(${_hd_dests[@]+"${_hd_dests[@]}"})
+      for d in ${dests[@]+"${dests[@]}"}; do
+        if _bdb_hd_exec_dest "$d" || _bdb_hd_same_line_exec "${d##*/}" "$i" $((i + 1)) $((found - 1)); then
+          cls=interpreter; break
+        fi
+      done
+    fi
+    _bdb_hd_scan_body $((i + 1)) $((found - 1)) "$_hd_quoted"
+    out="$out$l"$'\n'
+    if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]] && (( ! _hd_full )); then
+      # #1245 special case: a standalone quoted `cat <<'W' [> path]` drops it all.
+      if ! (( i == 0 && found == _bdb_hd_n - 1 && _hd_quoted )) || ! _bdb_hd_plain_cat "$l"; then
+        out="$out$_hd_kept"
+      fi
+    else
+      [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]] && cls=interpreter
+      for ((j = i + 1; j < found; j++)); do out="$out${_bdb_hd_L[j]}"$'\n'; done
+      out="$out$_hd_synth"
+    fi
+    out="$out${_bdb_hd_L[found]}"$'\n'
+    (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
+    case "$cls" in
+      interpreter) seen=interpreter ;;
+      none) [[ "$seen" == interpreter ]] || seen=none ;;
+      nonexec) [[ -n "$seen" ]] || seen=nonexec ;;
+    esac
+    i=$((found + 1))
+  done
+  _bdb_hd_class="${seen:-none}"
+  printf '%s' "${out%$'\n'}"
+}
+
+# The #1245 header grammar (byte-identical to _bdb_scrub_cat_heredoc's).
+_bdb_hd_plain_cat() {
+  local header="${1:-}" marker candidate
+  local delimiter_re="<<(-?)('([[:alnum:]_]+)'|\"([[:alnum:]_]+)\")"
+  local path_re="([[:alnum:]_./-]+|'[[:alnum:]_ ./-]+'|\"[[:alnum:]_ ./-]+\")"
+  local header_re="^[[:blank:]]*cat[[:blank:]]+(HEREDOC([[:blank:]]+>>?[[:blank:]]*${path_re})?|>>?[[:blank:]]*${path_re}[[:blank:]]+HEREDOC)[[:blank:]]*$"
+  [[ "$header" =~ $delimiter_re ]] || return 1
+  marker="${BASH_REMATCH[0]}"
+  candidate="${header/"$marker"/HEREDOC}"
+  [[ "$candidate" =~ $header_re ]]
+}

+# Knob: destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier in the repo's
+# .loa.config.yaml (read once, no fork, only for commands holding `<<`).
+# Only an explicit false|no|off turns it off; turning it off only tightens.
+_bdb_heredoc_knob_on() {
+  local cfg="${LOA_REPO_ROOT:-${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}}/.loa.config.yaml" content="" l in_blk=0
+  [[ -f "$cfg" && -r "$cfg" ]] || return 0
+  IFS= read -r -d '' content < "$cfg" || true
+  [[ "$content" == *heredoc_classifier* ]] || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r l; do
+    case "$l" in
+      destructive_command_guard:*) in_blk=1; continue ;;
+      [A-Za-z_]*) in_blk=0; continue ;;
+    esac
+    if (( in_blk )) && [[ "$l" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_knob ]]; then
+      case "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" in false|False|FALSE|no|No|NO|off|Off|OFF) return 1 ;; esac
+    fi
+  done <<< "$content"
+  return 0
+}
+
+# Exported entry points (source with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1).
+_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class() {
+  local LC_ALL=C
+  _bdb_heredoc_scrub "${1:-}" >/dev/null
+  printf '%s\n' "$_bdb_hd_class"
+}
+heredoc_nonexec() {
+  [[ "$(_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}")" == nonexec ]]
+}
+
+# Library mode: only when SOURCED. Executed with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 the hook runs
+# normally — an environment variable can never switch the fence off.
+if [[ "${BDB_LIB_ONLY:-}" == "1" && "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}" != "${0:-}" ]]; then
+  return 0
+fi

+# _bdb_hd_ctx_bad <line> → 0 when a line before (or the header itself) leaves

+# _bdb_hd_header <line> — parse one header line. Sets _hd_ops (heredoc count,
+# -1 = unreadable), _hd_delim, _hd_quoted, _hd_tabs, _hd_cls, _hd_dests[],
+# _hd_pipe (pipeline id of the heredoc on this line).
+_bdb_hd_header() {
+  local line="${1:-}" k nt t opi=-1 w seg=0 pipe=0
+  local -a tpipe mtoks
+  _hd_ops=0 _hd_delim="" _hd_quoted=0 _hd_tabs=0 _hd_cls=none _hd_pipe=-1
+  _hd_dests=()

+      '|'|'|&') tpipe[k]=-1; continue ;;
+    esac
+    tpipe[k]=$pipe
+    if [[ "$t" =~ ^[0-9]*'<<'-?$ ]]; then _hd_ops=$((_hd_ops + 1)); opi=$k; fi
+  done
+  (( _hd_ops == 1 )) || return
+  w="${_bdb_hd_tok[opi+1]:-}"
+  [[ "${_bdb_hd_tok[opi]}" == *'<<-' ]] && _hd_tabs=1
+  if [[ "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_dsq || "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ddq || "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_dbs ]]; then
+    _hd_delim="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"; _hd_quoted=1
+  elif [[ "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_dw ]]; then
+    _hd_delim="$w"
+  else
+    _hd_ops=-1; return        # variable-expanded, mixed or missing delimiter
+  fi
+  _hd_pipe="${tpipe[opi]}"
+  if _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$line"; then _hd_cls=interpreter; return; fi
+  _bdb_hd_tokenize "$line"    # _bdb_hd_ctx_bad reused the token buffer
+  # Classify every member of the heredoc's pipeline; the most executing wins.
+  local cls=nonexec
+  k=0
+  while (( k < nt )); do
+    if [[ "${tpipe[k]}" != "$_hd_pipe" ]]; then k=$((k + 1)); continue; fi
+    mtoks=()
+    while (( k < nt )) && [[ "${tpipe[k]}" == "$_hd_pipe" ]]; do mtoks[${#mtoks[@]}]="${_bdb_hd_tok[k]}"; k=$((k + 1)); done
+    _bdb_hd_member "${mtoks[@]}"
+    case "$_hd_mcls" in
+      interpreter) cls=interpreter ;;
+      none) [[ "$cls" == interpreter ]] || cls=none ;;
+    esac
+    k=$((k + 1))
+  done
+  _hd_cls="$cls"
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_segword <segment> → _hd_w (command word after wrapper stripping,
+# quotes and an absolute path removed) and _hd_rest (the text after it).
+_bdb_hd_segword() {
+  local s="${1:-}" w guard=0
+  _hd_w="" _hd_rest=""
+  while (( guard < 64 )); do
+    guard=$((guard + 1))
+    s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
+    [[ -n "$s" ]] || return
+    case "${s:0:1}" in
+      '('|'{'|'!'|'\'|'"'|"'") s="${s:1}"; continue ;;
+    esac
+    w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"
+    s="${s:${#w}}"
+    if [[ "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_assign ]]; then continue; fi
+    case "$w" in
+      sudo|doas|command|exec|env|nice|time|nohup|builtin|stdbuf|ionice)
+        while :; do
+          s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
+          case "$s" in
+            -S|-S[[:space:]]*|--split-string*) _hd_w="sh"; _hd_rest="$s"; return ;;
+            -[ugnCphUrtTDc]|-[ugnCphUrtTDc][[:space:]]*)
+              s="${s:2}"; s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"; s="${s:${#w}}" ;;
+            -*) w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"; s="${s:${#w}}" ;;
+            *) break ;;
+          esac
+        done
+        continue ;;
+    esac
+    w="${w%%[\"\']*}"
+    [[ "$w" == */* && "$w" != '$'* ]] && w="${w##*/}"
+    _hd_w="$w"; _hd_rest="$s"
+    return
+  done
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_scan_body <first> <last> <quoted> — per-segment scan of
+# _bdb_hd_L[first..last]. Sets _hd_kept (fence-verb segments, one per line),
+# _hd_synth (variable-command segments rewritten as rm/git/kubectl) and
+# _hd_full (1 = the body needs the full scan).
+_bdb_hd_scan_body() {
+  local k l t seg
+  _hd_kept="" _hd_synth="" _hd_full=0
+  for ((k = $1; k <= $2; k++)); do
+    l="${_bdb_hd_L[k]}"
+    [[ "$l" == *'<<'* ]] && _hd_full=1
+    if (( ! $3 )); then
+      case "$l" in *'$('*|*'`'*|*'<('*|*'>('*) _hd_full=1 ;; esac
+    fi
+    t="${l//'&&'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//'||'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//'|'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//';'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//'&'/$'\n'}"
+    while :; do
+      seg="${t%%$'\n'*}"
+      _bdb_hd_segword "$seg"
+      if [[ -n "$_hd_w" ]]; then
+        if [[ "$_hd_w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_varw ]]; then
+          _hd_full=1
+          _hd_synth="${_hd_synth}rm${_hd_rest}"$'\n'"git${_hd_rest}"$'\n'"kubectl${_hd_rest}"$'\n'
+        elif _bdb_hd_is_destructive "$_hd_w"; then
+          _hd_kept="${_hd_kept}${_hd_w}${_hd_rest}"$'\n'
+        elif _bdb_hd_is_interp "$_hd_w" || _bdb_hd_is_runner "$_hd_w"; then
+          _hd_full=1
+        fi
+      fi
+      [[ "$t" == *$'\n'* ]] || break
+      t="${t#*$'\n'}"
+    done
+  done
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_same_line_exec <basename> <header idx> <body first> <body last>
+# → 0 when the target is named anywhere else in the command outside a safe
+# reader (it may be executed, sourced, made executable, copied or moved).
+_bdb_hd_same_line_exec() {
+  local b="$1" hi="$2" bf="$3" bl="$4" k nt t u c cw seg_has pipe start j own
+  for ((k = 0; k < _bdb_hd_n; k++)); do
+    (( k >= bf && k <= bl )) && continue
+    [[ "${_bdb_hd_L[k]}" == *"$b"* ]] || continue
+    _bdb_hd_tokenize "${_bdb_hd_L[k]}" || return 0
+    nt=${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}
+    start=0 pipe=0
+    for ((j = 0; j <= nt; j++)); do
+      t="${_bdb_hd_tok[j]:-}"
+      if (( j < nt )) && ! [[ "$t" =~ ^(';'|';;'|'&'|'&&'|'||'|'('|')'|'|'|'|&')$ ]]; then continue; fi
+      # segment [start, j)
+      own=0
+      (( k == hi && pipe == _hd_pipe_saved )) && own=1
+      if (( ! own )); then
+        seg_has=0 cw=""
+        for ((c = start; c < j; c++)); do
+          u="${_bdb_hd_tok[c]}"; u="${u//[\"\']/}"; u="${u##*/}"
+          [[ "$u" == "$b" ]] && seg_has=1
+        done
+        if (( seg_has )); then
+          _bdb_hd_segword "${_bdb_hd_tok[*]:start:j-start}"
+          cw="$_hd_w"
+          if ! _bdb_hd_is_safe_reader "$cw" || [[ "$cw" == "$b" ]]; then return 0; fi
+        fi
+      fi
+      case "$t" in '|'|'|&') ;; *) pipe=$((pipe + 1)) ;; esac
+      start=$((j + 1))
+    done
+  done
+  return 1
+}
+
+# _bdb_heredoc_scrub <command> — print the scrub copy (non-executing heredoc
+# bodies reduced to their fence-verb segments) and set _bdb_hd_class to the
+# most executing class seen (interpreter > none > nonexec; none if no heredoc).
+_bdb_heredoc_scrub() {
+  local text="${1:-}" out="" i j found l cls ctx=0 seen="" d first
+  _bdb_hd_class=none
+  text="${text//$'\r\n'/$'\n'}"
+  if [[ "$text" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ctl ]]; then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
+  text="${text%$'\n'}"
+  _bdb_hd_L=()
+  while IFS= read -r l; do _bdb_hd_L[${#_bdb_hd_L[@]}]="$l"; done <<< "$text"
+  _bdb_hd_n=${#_bdb_hd_L[@]}
+  i=0
+  while (( i < _bdb_hd_n )); do
+    l="${_bdb_hd_L[i]}"
+    if [[ "$l" != *'<<'* ]]; then
+      out="$out$l"$'\n'
+      (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
+      i=$((i + 1)); continue
+    fi
+    _bdb_hd_header "$l"
+    if (( _hd_ops == 0 )); then
+      out="$out$l"$'\n'
+      (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
+      i=$((i + 1)); continue
+    fi
+    if (( _hd_ops != 1 )); then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
+    found=-1
+    for ((j = i + 1; j < _bdb_hd_n; j++)); do
+      d="${_bdb_hd_L[j]}"
+      if (( _hd_tabs )); then while [[ "$d" == $'\t'* ]]; do d="${d#$'\t'}"; done; fi
+      if [[ "$d" == "$_hd_delim" ]]; then found=$j; break; fi
+    done
+    if (( found < 0 )); then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
+    cls="$_hd_cls"
+    (( ctx )) && cls=interpreter
+    _hd_pipe_saved="$_hd_pipe"
+    if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]]; then
+      first="${_bdb_hd_L[i+1]:-}"
+      (( i + 1 < found )) || first=""
+      first="${first#"${first%%[![:blank:]]*}"}"
+      [[ "$first" == '#!'* ]] && cls=interpreter
+    fi
+    if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]]; then
+      local -a dests
+      dests=(${_hd_dests[@]+"${_hd_dests[@]}"})
+      for d in ${dests[@]+"${dests[@]}"}; do
+        if _bdb_hd_exec_dest "$d" || _bdb_hd_same_line_exec "${d##*/}" "$i" $((i + 1)) $((found - 1)); then
+          cls=interpreter; break
+        fi
+      done
+    fi
+    _bdb_hd_scan_body $((i + 1)) $((found - 1)) "$_hd_quoted"
+    out="$out$l"$'\n'
+    if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]] && (( ! _hd_full )); then
+      # #1245 special case: a standalone quoted `cat <<'W' [> path]` drops it all.
+      if ! (( i == 0 && found == _bdb_hd_n - 1 && _hd_quoted )) || ! _bdb_hd_plain_cat "$l"; then
+        out="$out$_hd_kept"
+      fi
+    else
+      [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]] && cls=interpreter
+      for ((j = i + 1; j < found; j++)); do out="$out${_bdb_hd_L[j]}"$'\n'; done
+      out="$out$_hd_synth"
+    fi
+    out="$out${_bdb_hd_L[found]}"$'\n'
+    (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
+    case "$cls" in
+      interpreter) seen=interpreter ;;
+      none) [[ "$seen" == interpreter ]] || seen=none ;;
+      nonexec) [[ -n "$seen" ]] || seen=nonexec ;;
+    esac
+    i=$((found + 1))
+  done
+  _bdb_hd_class="${seen:-none}"
+  printf '%s' "${out%$'\n'}"
+}
+
+# The #1245 header grammar (byte-identical to _bdb_scrub_cat_heredoc's).
+_bdb_hd_plain_cat() {
+  local header="${1:-}" marker candidate
+  local delimiter_re="<<(-?)('([[:alnum:]_]+)'|\"([[:alnum:]_]+)\")"
+  local path_re="([[:alnum:]_./-]+|'[[:alnum:]_ ./-]+'|\"[[:alnum:]_ ./-]+\")"
+  local header_re="^[[:blank:]]*cat[[:blank:]]+(HEREDOC([[:blank:]]+>>?[[:blank:]]*${path_re})?|>>?[[:blank:]]*${path_re}[[:blank:]]+HEREDOC)[[:blank:]]*$"
+  [[ "$header" =~ $delimiter_re ]] || return 1
+  marker="${BASH_REMATCH[0]}"
+  candidate="${header/"$marker"/HEREDOC}"
+  [[ "$candidate" =~ $header_re ]]
+}
+
+# Knob: destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier in the repo's
+# .loa.config.yaml (read once, no fork, only for commands holding `<<`).
+# Only an explicit false|no|off turns it off; turning it off only tightens.
+_bdb_heredoc_knob_on() {
+  local cfg="${LOA_REPO_ROOT:-${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}}/.loa.config.yaml" content="" l in_blk=0
+  [[ -f "$cfg" && -r "$cfg" ]] || return 0
+  IFS= read -r -d '' content < "$cfg" || true
+  [[ "$content" == *heredoc_classifier* ]] || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r l; do
+    case "$l" in
+      destructive_command_guard:*) in_blk=1; continue ;;
+      [A-Za-z_]*) in_blk=0; continue ;;
+    esac
+    if (( in_blk )) && [[ "$l" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_knob ]]; then
+      case "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" in false|False|FALSE|no|No|NO|off|Off|OFF) return 1 ;; esac
+    fi
+  done <<< "$content"
+  return 0
+}
+
+# Exported entry points (source with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1).
+_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class() {
+  local LC_ALL=C
+  _bdb_heredoc_scrub "${1:-}" >/dev/null
+  printf '%s\n' "$_bdb_hd_class"
+}
+heredoc_nonexec() {
+  [[ "$(_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}")" == nonexec ]]
+}
+
+# Library mode: only when SOURCED. Executed with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 the hook runs
+# normally — an environment variable can never switch the fence off.
+if [[ "${BDB_LIB_ONLY:-}" == "1" && "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}" != "${0:-}" ]]; then
+  return 0
+fi
+
 # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 # jq presence probe (SDD §6.5 — SKP-008 mitigation, not full fix).
 # If jq is absent, the input parse on line ~120 returns empty → existing
@@ -412,7 +1055,16 @@ _cmd_match="$command"
 if [[ "$_cmd_match" == *"for "* || "$_cmd_match" == *"python"* ]]; then
   _cmd_match=$(_bdb_scrub_literal_program "$_cmd_match")
 fi
-[[ "$_cmd_match" == *"<<"* ]] && _cmd_match=$(_bdb_scrub_cat_heredoc "$_cmd_match")
+# cycle-129 FR-6: with destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier on (the
+# default) the fail-closed consumer classifier above replaces the #1245 scrub,
+# which survives unchanged as its special case and as the knob-off path.
+if [[ "$_cmd_match" == *"<<"* ]]; then
+  if _bdb_heredoc_knob_on; then
+    _cmd_match=$(_bdb_heredoc_scrub "$_cmd_match")
+  else
+    _cmd_match=$(_bdb_scrub_cat_heredoc "$_cmd_match")
+  fi
+fi
 [[ "$_cmd_match" == *"git"* ]] && _cmd_match=$(_bdb_scrub "$_bdb_re_git" "$_cmd_match")
 if [[ "$_cmd_match" == *"br "* || "$_cmd_match" == *"bd "* ]]; then
   _cmd_match=$(_bdb_scrub "$_bdb_re_brbd" "$_cmd_match")
diff --git a/.claude/hooks/session-start/loa-decisions-surface.sh b/.claude/hooks/session-start/loa-decisions-surface.sh

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# PreToolUse:Bash Safety Hook — Block Destructive Commands (v1.38.0)
# =============================================================================
# Blocks dangerous patterns and suggests safer alternatives.
# Exit 0 = allow, Exit 2 = block (stderr message fed back to agent).
#
# Cycle-111 (sprint-164, 2026-05-16) — ports Anthropic DCG public pattern
# set inline. Source: github.com/anthropics/destructive-command-guard
# Pattern port reference SHA: HEAD as of 2026-05-16 (no specific commit
# pin available — DCG ships rule packs, not single-file source).
# REVIEW-BY: 2026-08-16 — re-sync against upstream DCG every quarter.
#
# IMPORTANT: No set -euo pipefail — this hook must never fail closed.
# A grep or jq failure must result in exit 0 (allow), not an error.
#
# WHY fail-open (not fail-closed): A safety hook that crashes or encounters
# a parse error must NOT block the agent from operating. The alternative —
# fail-closed — would make jq/grep bugs into denial-of-service attacks
# against the agent. Fail-open with logging is the standard pattern for
# inline security hooks (cf. ModSecurity DetectionOnly mode).
# (Source: bridge-20260213-c011he iter-1 HIGH-1 fix)
#
# WHY GNU/BSD ERE (NOT strict POSIX): grep -P (PCRE) is a GNU extension not
# available on macOS/BSD or minimal containers. grep -E (Extended Regex)
# with `\s`, `\S`, `\b` extensions works on both GNU grep (Linux) and BSD
# grep (macOS Sonoma+). Strict-POSIX ERE (busybox without -E extensions)
# is NOT in scope per cycle-111 SDD §5.0 honest-scope decision.
# (Source: bridge-20260213-c011he iter-1 HIGH-1 fix; cycle-111 SDD §5.0)
#
# WHY single script for all patterns: NFR-5 single-file invariant. Multiple
# hooks would each read stdin, parse JSON, and run regex — multiplying
# latency per command. A single emit_block helper with sequential patterns
# is simpler and faster. (cycle-111 SDD §5/§6.)
#
# Defense-in-depth posture (cycle-111 SDD §11): this hook is a fence
# against routine destructive-command mistakes by autonomous agents, NOT
# a hardened security boundary against intentional bypass. Known accepted
# bypass classes: newline statement separators, subshell wrapping
# (`bash -c '...'`, `$(...)`), eval/base64 decode, SQL comments containing
# WHERE, jq absent from PATH. See SDD §11 for full table.
# Current executable limit examples and issue dispositions:
# docs/runbooks/hook-safety.md (#1047, #1245, #1088, #1031).
#
# cycle-125 FR-1 (2026-09-23) — precision pass against the fleet corpus
# (tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/, replayed by tests/unit/block-destructive-
# bash.bats). Relaxations, each on a positively established predicate:
# FR-2 cache/build vocabulary by last segment, bare names after a
# statement-initial `cd <temp>`, paths strictly below /tmp|/var/tmp|
# /private/tmp, `$TMPDIR/<name>` only with a real temp TMPDIR, a variable
# bound exactly once to `$(mktemp -d)`; FR-1.1 branches that are ancestors
# of main/master (offline `git merge-base`); FR-1.3 generated paths;
# FR-1.4/5/6 only when a SQL runner (psql, mysql, sqlite3, prisma, …) or an
# inline interpreter program (`python -c`, `node -e`) is in the command.
# ACCEPTED RESIDUALS (deliberately not relaxed):
#   * Remote payloads: `ssh host 'rm -rf /'`, `docker exec c rm -rf /data`,
#     `kubectl exec p -- rm -rf /` keep blocking. A scrub of quoted remote
#     payloads was withdrawn at design time (Flatline SKP-001) — the text
#     fence cannot tell a remote target from a local one, and the blast
#     radius of a remote wipe is larger, not smaller.
#   * SQL through a script FILE (`python app.py` that drops a table) was
#     never matched and still is not; inline programs are matched by text.
#   * `cd "$(mktemp -d)" && rm -rf out` (substitution as the cd target) and
#     `rm -rf "$T"` where T came from anything but a plain `$(mktemp -d)`
#     or a temp path stay blocked — bind the path first, then rm.
#   * The hook never consults its own $PWD: a project checked out under
#     /tmp still has `rm -rf src` blocked.
#   * Rebinding builtins void the once-bound-variable proof only in command
#     position (`read T`, `while read T`, `IFS= read -r T`, `command read`,
#     `eval "read T"`); `exec read`, `env … read`, `sudo read`, `nice read`
#     are NOT counted — `read` is a builtin, so those forms fail or run in a
#     child and cannot rebind the caller's variable. `notes-guard.sh read`
#     and `echo read` are arguments, never rebinds.
#
# Registered in settings.hooks.json as PreToolUse matcher: "Bash"
# Part of Loa Harness Engineering (cycle-011, issue #297)
# Source: Trail of Bits claude-code-config safety patterns
# =============================================================================
# perf pass-2 (2026-07-05, skill-loop): fork/exec reduction. The boolean
# `echo | grep -qE` pattern dispatches (15 spawns on every benign Bash call)
# are replaced by bash [[ =~ ]] via the _match/_match_ci helpers below, which
# preserve grep's PER-LINE match model byte-for-byte (see helper comments).
# `\b` was translated to explicit POSIX boundary classes because bash =~
# compiles with the SYSTEM regex library — glibc supports \b, BSD libc does
# NOT, and this hook commits to macOS/BSD (header above). Each translated
# pattern carries an equivalence note. Deliberately NOT converted (grep
# retained): P10 DELETE-FROM segment extraction (grep -oiE multi-match with
# original-case output is not provably reproducible in bash — no match-offset
# primitive), the FR-SZ inner write-intent tests (their `X\b[^|;&]*` shapes
# make consuming \b-translation non-isomorphic; they only run when the
# command already mentions a protected path), and all `grep -oE | head -1`
# matched-substring extractions (block path only — the hook exits 2 right
# after). Also: stdin now streams straight into the Path-A jq (no cat spawn),
# audit timestamps use printf %(...)T (no date spawn), cwd uses $PWD.
# =============================================================================
# perf pass-8 (2026-07-05, skill-loop): provably-complete literal pre-filters
# on the pattern dispatch. After pass 2 the ~95% benign path still paid 13
# sequential ERE evaluations (~0.4 ms) plus the one unconditional P10 grep
# spawn (~3 ms). Each pattern group is now guarded by a cheap bash substring
# test on literal(s) PROVABLY NECESSARY for the group to match: each guard
# literal appears in the group's regex as a mandatory concatenation element —
# outside every alternation branch, optional (?) group and starred group — so
# any MATCHING LINE must contain it verbatim, hence the whole $command must
# contain it. Absence from the whole string therefore proves no line can
# match, and the group is skipped — outcome-identical by construction.
# Where a guard uses an alternation's literals (P6 drop|clear, FR-SZ
# .run/|grimoires/loa/skills), the guard tests ALL branch literals and any
# hit evaluates the group. Guards only ever SKIP, never accept: when the
# literal is present the group evaluates exactly as before, in the original
# order (first match still wins, block messages byte-identical).
# Case-insensitive groups (P8/P9/P10) guard on the same C-locale ASCII fold
# (${command,,}) that _match_ci applies per line and grep -i applies under
# the LC_ALL=C pin — folding is per-character and leaves \n untouched, so
# the folded whole string is exactly the folded lines joined by \n, and a
# literal absent from the folded whole is absent from every folded line.
# Per-group necessity proofs sit next to each guard. The P10 DELETE-FROM
# grep — the last unconditional spawn on the benign path — now runs only
# when the folded command contains both "delete" and "from" (both mandatory
# in its -i pattern). The log-redactor stays block-path-only (verified: it
# is exec'd only inside emit_block and the FR-SZ bypass audit branch).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# jq presence probe (SDD §6.5 — SKP-008 mitigation, not full fix).
# If jq is absent, the input parse on line ~120 returns empty → existing
# fail-open guard exits 0. v1.38.0 adds a one-shot stderr WARNING so the
# operator / agent sees the safety guard is disabled this session.
# Tracked as cycle-112 candidate (filesystem-marker variant for cross-
# invocation persistence; env-var doesn't propagate across hook subprocess
# invocations per Flatline SKP-002 round-3 finding).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# perf pass-11 (skill-loop, 2026-07-06): HIGH-002 fix (BB review of PR #1176).
# Passes 2 & 8 introduced bash-4-only constructs into this fence (${x,,}
# case-folding, `mapfile`); pre-loop it was bash-3.2-portable (echo|grep -i).
# macOS ships bash 3.2. This guard runs BEFORE any bash-4 expansion executes
# (bash 3.2 defers ${,,} validation and the mapfile builtin lookup to runtime,
# so a runtime guard at the first executable line runs first and never reaches
# them). If a bash >=4 exists (the framework already requires it — beads-health
# etc. source bash-version-guard.sh), re-exec under it; stdin (the hook payload)
# and argv survive exec. Otherwise FAIL CLOSED (exit 2 = block): a
# destructive-command fence must never silently allow when it cannot evaluate.
# The generic bash-version-guard.sh exits 1, which is a NON-blocking PreToolUse
# hook error (fail-OPEN) — wrong direction for this hook, hence the inline form.
if [ "${BASH_VERSINFO:-0}" -lt 4 ]; then
    for _bh_cand in /opt/homebrew/bin/bash /usr/local/bin/bash /usr/bin/bash bash; do

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# heredoc-classifier.sh — library entry points for the FR-6 heredoc consumer
+# classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1). The single implementation lives in the fence,
+# .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh; this file sources it in
+# library mode (BDB_LIB_ONLY=1, which the fence honours only when sourced) so
+# other scripts — guard-yield.sh's likely-false-positive heuristic — can call:
+#
+#   heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   prints interpreter|nonexec|none
+#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>          exit 0 iff the command's heredocs
+#                                           all have non-executing consumers
+#
+# Source only; never execute. Bash 3.2 compatible. When the fence cannot be
+# read the functions report "none" / exit 1, which callers treat as "no
+# classifier" (guard-yield.sh falls back to `<<` presence).
+_hc_lib_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+_hc_fence="${_hc_lib_dir}/../../hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
+if [[ -r "$_hc_fence" ]]; then
+  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
+  BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 source "$_hc_fence"
+fi
+unset _hc_lib_dir _hc_fence
+
+heredoc_consumer_class() {
+  if declare -F _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}"
+  else
+    printf 'none\n'
+  fi
+}
+
+heredoc_nonexec() {
+  [[ "$(heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}")" == nonexec ]]
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# heredoc-classifier.sh — library entry points for the FR-6 heredoc consumer
+# classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1). The single implementation lives in the fence,
+# .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh; this file sources it in
+# library mode (BDB_LIB_ONLY=1, which the fence honours only when sourced) so
+# other scripts — guard-yield.sh's likely-false-positive heuristic — can call:
+#
+#   heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   prints interpreter|nonexec|none
+#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>          exit 0 iff the command's heredocs
+#                                           all have non-executing consumers
+#
+# Source only; never execute. Bash 3.2 compatible. When the fence cannot be
+# read the functions report "none" / exit 1, which callers treat as "no
+# classifier" (guard-yield.sh falls back to `<<` presence).
+_hc_lib_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+_hc_fence="${_hc_lib_dir}/../../hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
+if [[ -r "$_hc_fence" ]]; then
+  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
+  BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 source "$_hc_fence"
+fi
+unset _hc_lib_dir _hc_fence
+
+heredoc_consumer_class() {
+  if declare -F _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}"
+  else
+    printf 'none\n'
+  fi
+}
+
+heredoc_nonexec() {
+  [[ "$(heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}")" == nonexec ]]
+}

+# fb_parse FILE GATE → one compact JSON object: {file, exists, trailer, verdict,
+# counts, exit_code, sprint_id, ts, approved, hash}. The hash is the run-mode
+# same-issue hash (md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` over verdict-derive's
+# --json output; legacy files hash their findings section).
+fb_parse() {
+  local f="$1" g="$2" rel vj tl pj hash
+  rel="${f#"$root"/}"
+  if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then jq -nc --arg f "$rel" '{file: $f, exists: false}'; return 0; fi
+  vj=$(bash "$VERDICT_DERIVE" --file "$f" --gate "$g" --json 2>/dev/null) || true
+  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$vj" || vj='{"trailer_found":false,"verdict":null,"counts":null,"exit_code":1}'
+  tl=$(grep -E '^<!-- LOA-VERDICT \{.*\} -->[[:space:]]*$' "$f" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1) || tl=""
+  pj=$(printf '%s' "$tl" | sed -E 's/^<!-- LOA-VERDICT (.*) -->[[:space:]]*$/\1/')
+  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$pj" || pj='{}'
+  if [[ "$(jq -r '.trailer_found' <<<"$vj")" == true ]]; then
+    hash=$(printf '%s\n' "$vj" | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)
+  else
+    hash=$( { grep -A 100 "## Findings\|## Issues\|## Changes Required" "$f" 2>/dev/null || true; } | head -50 | _md5)
+  fi
+  jq -nc --arg f "$rel" --argjson v "$vj" --argjson p "$pj" --arg h "$hash" '
+    def sid: if type == "string" and test("^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$") then . else null end;
+    def tsv: if type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$") then . else null end;
+    {file: $f, exists: true, trailer: ($v.trailer_found == true),
+     verdict: ($v.verdict | if type == "string" then . else null end),
+     counts: ($v.counts // null), exit_code: ($v.exit_code // 1),
+     sprint_id: ($p.sprint_id | sid), ts: ($p.ts | tsv), hash: $h}
+    | .approved = (.exit_code == 0 and .verdict == "APPROVED")'
+}

+# SINCE touching a path outside the state/generated set, or nothing
+impl_commit() {
+  git -C "$root" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  git -C "$root" log --no-merges -n 1 --format='%H %ct' ${1:+"--since=$1"} -- . \
+    ':(exclude,glob)grimoires/**' ':(exclude,glob).run/**' ':(exclude,glob)**/REPO-MAP.md' \
+    ':(exclude,glob)**/checksums.json' ':(exclude,glob)**/CHANGELOG.md' 2>/dev/null || true
+}
+
+# The ordered rounds of one sprint directory: every -rN file, then the current
+# file unless it is byte-identical to the highest -rN of its gate
+rounds_of() {
+  local dir="$1" g base f n top topn cur
+  for g in review audit; do
+    if [[ "$g" == review ]]; then base=engineer-feedback; else base=auditor-sprint-feedback; fi
+    top=""; topn=-1
+    for f in "$dir/$base"-r*.md; do
+      [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
+      n=${f##*-r}; n=${n%.md}
+      [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]{1,6}$ ]] || continue
+      fb_parse "$f" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" --argjson n "$((10#$n))" '. + {gate: $g, round: $n}'
+      if (( 10#$n > topn )); then topn=$((10#$n)); top="$f"; fi
+    done
+    cur="$dir/$base.md"
+    if [[ -f "$cur" ]] && ! { [[ -n "$top" ]] && cmp -s "$cur" "$top"; }; then
+      fb_parse "$cur" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" '. + {gate: $g, round: 999999}'
+    fi
+  done
+}
+
+# Shared jq definitions: time, the breaker recompute and the run-state resolution
+JQ_DEFS='
+def epoch: if type == "string" then (sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch null) else null end;
+def fresh($now; $win): epoch as $t | $t != null and ($now - $t) <= $win and ($t - $now) <= 300;
+def recompute($rounds; $reset):
+  ($rounds
+   | map(select($reset == null or ((.ts // "") > $reset)))
+   | sort_by([(.ts // ""), .round, (if .gate == "review" then 0 else 1 end)])
+   | map(select(.approved | not))) as $nr
+  | reduce $nr[] as $r ({cycle: 0, same: 0, hash: null, np: 0, lc: null};
+      .cycle += 1
+      | (if $r.hash != "none" and $r.hash == .hash then .same += 1 else .same = 1 | .hash = $r.hash end)
+      | ($r.counts | tojson) as $c
+      | (if .lc != null and .lc == $c then .np += 1 else .np = 0 end)
+      | .lc = $c);
+def skeleton($th; $ts):
+  {state: "CLOSED",
+   triggers: {same_issue: {count: 0, threshold: $th.same, last_hash: null},
+              no_progress: {count: 0, threshold: $th.np},
+              cycle_count: {current: 0, limit: $th.cycles},
+              timeout: {started: $ts, limit_hours: $th.hours}},
+   history: []};
+def merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts):
+  (if type == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
+  | .triggers = (.triggers // {})
+  | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ([(.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0), $rc.cycle] | max)
+  | (if $rc.same > (.triggers.same_issue.count // 0)
+     then .triggers.same_issue.count = $rc.same | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $rc.hash else . end)
+  | (if $rc.np > (.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) or (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts == null and $rc.lc != null)
+     then .triggers.no_progress.count = ([(.triggers.no_progress.count // 0), $rc.np] | max)
+          | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $rc.lc else . end)
+  | ( if (.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
+        then ["same_issue", "same issue hash repeated \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times (derived from the feedback history)"]
+      elif (.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
+        then ["no_progress", "counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds (derived from the feedback history)"]
+      elif (.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
+        then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds (derived from the feedback history)"]
+      else null end ) as $trip
+  | if $trip != null and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
+    then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], source: "derive"}])
+    else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end;
+def known_ids: (.derivation.sprint_ids // null) // ((.sprints.list // []) | map(.id? // empty));
+def resolve($f; $now; $win):
+  . as $c
+  | (if ($c | type) == "object" then $c else {} end) as $c
+  | ($c.state // $c.status // "") as $cs
+  | ($c | known_ids) as $known
+  | ([$f.sprints[] | select(.state != "complete")
+      | "sprint-\(.global_id)" as $g | .local_label as $l
+      | select(($known | index($g)) == null and ($l == "" or ($known | index($l)) == null))] | length > 0) as $new
+  | ((($c.completion // {}) | .merged_sha? // "") | type == "string" and length > 0) as $merged
+  | if ($c.state // "") == "JACKED_OUT" or ($c.status // "") == "JACKED_OUT" or $merged then "JACKED_OUT"
+    elif $f.breaker_open or $cs == "HALTED" then "HALTED"
+    elif $f.all_complete then "COMPLETE"
+    elif $cs == "COMPLETE" and ($new | not) then "COMPLETE"
+    elif ($c.timestamps.last_activity? // null) | fresh($now; $win) then "RUNNING"
+    else "INTERRUPTED" end;
+'
+
+cmd_derive() {
+  local ledger="$root/grimoires/loa/ledger.json" a2a="$root/grimoires/loa/a2a" active rows
+  if [[ ! -f "$ledger" ]] || ! jq -e 'type == "object"' "$ledger" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "run-checkpoint: derive: no readable ledger at $ledger — callers keep the cache" >&2; return 4
+  fi
+  active=$(jq -r '.active_cycle // empty | strings' "$ledger")
+  if [[ -z "$active" ]] || ! jq -e --arg c "$active" 'any(.cycles[]?; .id == $c)' "$ledger" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "run-checkpoint: derive: the ledger has no active cycle — callers keep the cache" >&2; return 4
+  fi
+  local win now now_ts fa=1 th
+  win=$(( $(cfg_int '.run_mode.stale_hours' 12 8760) * 3600 ))
+  [[ "$(cfg '.run_mode.file_authoritative')" == false ]] && fa=0
+  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
+              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \
+              --argjson c "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.max_cycles' 20 10000)" \
+              --argjson h "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.timeout_hours' 8 8760)" \
+              '{same: $s, np: $n, cycles: $c, hours: $h}')
+  now=$(date +%s); now_ts=$(now_iso)
+
+  # Per-sprint facts
+  local sprints="[]" gid label lstatus since dir rv au mex msid ic sj
+  rows=$(jq -r --arg c "$active" '
+    (.cycles[] | select(.id == $c)) as $cy
+    | ($cy.sprints // [])[]
+    | select((.global_id | type) == "number")
+    | [(.global_id | tostring), ((.local_label // "") | tostring), ((.status // "") | tostring),
+       ([.started, .created, $cy.created] | map(select(type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-")))
+        | if length == 0 then "" else ([.[0], ($cy.created // "")] | max) end)]
+    | map(if . == "" then "-" else . end)
+    | @tsv' "$ledger")
+  # "-" stands for an empty field: IFS whitespace (tab) would collapse two adjacent separators
+  while IFS=$'\t' read -r gid label lstatus since; do
+    [[ "$gid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
+    [[ "$label" == - ]] && label=""
+    [[ "$since" == - ]] && since=""
+    [[ "$label" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$ ]] || label=""
+    [[ "$lstatus" =~ ^[a-z_]{1,32}$ ]] || lstatus="unknown"
+    [[ "$since" =~ ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$ ]] || since=""
+    dir="$a2a/sprint-$gid"
+    rv=$(fb_parse "$dir/engineer-feedback.md" review)
+    au=$(fb_parse "$dir/auditor-sprint-feedback.md" audit)
+    mex=false; msid=""
+    if [[ -f "$dir/COMPLETED" ]]; then
+      mex=true
+      msid=$(sed -n 's/^sprint:[[:space:]]*\([A-Za-z0-9._-]*\).*/\1/p' "$dir/COMPLETED" | head -n 1) || msid=""
+    fi
+    ic=$(impl_commit "$since")
+    sj=$(jq -nc --argjson gid "$gid" --arg label "$label" --arg status "$lstatus" --argjson rv "$rv" --argjson au "$au" \
+              --argjson mex "$mex" --arg msid "$msid" --arg ic "$ic" '
+      def mine: type == "string" and length > 0 and (. == "sprint-\($gid)" or ($label != "" and . == $label));
+      ($rv.approved == true and ($rv.sprint_id | mine)) as $R
+      | ($au.approved == true and ($au.sprint_id | mine)) as $A
+      | ([$rv.sprint_id, $au.sprint_id, (if $msid == "" then null else $msid end)] | map(select(type == "string" and length > 0))) as $ids
+      | ($mex and any($ids[]; mine | not)) as $stale
+      | ($mex and ($stale | not) and (($rv.sprint_id | mine) or ($au.sprint_id | mine))) as $M
+      | ($ic | split(" ")) as $c
+      | ([$rv.ts, $au.ts] | map(select(. != null)) | max) as $vts
+      | def verdict($x): if $x.exists then {verdict: $x.verdict, sprint_id: $x.sprint_id, consistent: ($x.exit_code == 0), file: $x.file} else null end;
+      {global_id: $gid, local_label: $label, status: $status,
+       completed_marker: $M, marker_present: $mex, stale_marker: $stale,
+       review: verdict($rv), audit: verdict($au),
+       impl_commit: (if ($c | length) == 2 then $c[0] else null end),
+       commit_after_verdict: (if ($c | length) == 2 and $vts != null
+                              then (($c[1] | tonumber) > ($vts | sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch 0)) else null end),
+       legacy_feedback: ([$rv, $au] | map(select(.exists and (.trailer | not)) | .file)),
+       state: (if $M and $R and $A and $status == "completed" then "complete"
+               elif ($M | not) and $R and $A then "awaiting_marker" else "in_progress" end)}')
+    sprints=$(jq -c --argjson s "$sj" '. + [$s]' <<<"$sprints")
+  done <<<"$rows"
+
+  # Breaker recompute over the active sprint's ordered rounds
+  local active_gid rounds cache="null" cache_ok=1 bcache="null" reset rc merged
+  active_gid=$(jq -r 'if length == 0 then "" else ((map(select(.state != "complete")) | .[0]) // .[-1]) | .global_id | tostring end' <<<"$sprints")
+  rounds="[]"
+  if [[ -n "$active_gid" && -d "$a2a/sprint-$active_gid" ]]; then
+    rounds=$(rounds_of "$a2a/sprint-$active_gid" | jq -sc '.')
+  fi
+  if [[ -f "$file" ]]; then
+    if cache=$(jq -c . "$file" 2>/dev/null) && [[ -n "$cache" ]]; then :; else cache="null"; cache_ok=0; fi
+  fi
+  if [[ -f "$breaker" ]]; then bcache=$(jq -c 'if type == "object" then . else null end' "$breaker" 2>/dev/null) || bcache="null"; [[ -n "$bcache" ]] || bcache="null"; fi
+  reset=$(jq -c '.reset_at? // null | if type == "string" then . else null end' <<<"$bcache")
+  rc=$(jq -nc --argjson r "$rounds" --argjson z "$reset" "$JQ_DEFS"' recompute($r; $z)')
+  merged=$(jq -c --argjson rc "$rc" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"' merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts)' <<<"$bcache")
+
+  local facts report
+  facts=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$sprints" --argjson b "$merged" '
+    {sprints: $s,
+     all_complete: (($s | length) > 0 and all($s[]; .state == "complete")),
+     breaker_open: ($b.state == "OPEN"),
+     stale_markers: [$s[] | select(.stale_marker) | "sprint-\(.global_id)"],
+     legacy_feedback: [$s[] | .legacy_feedback[]],
+     sprint_ids: [$s[] | "sprint-\(.global_id)"]}')
+  report=$(jq -nc --argjson f "$facts" --argjson c "$cache" --argjson b "$merged" --argjson rc "$rc" \
+                  --argjson now "$now" --argjson win "$win" --arg ts "$now_ts" --arg cycle "$active" \
+                  --argjson fa "$fa" --argjson cache_ok "$cache_ok" --arg ag "$active_gid" "$JQ_DEFS"'
+    def st: if type == "string" then (if test("^[A-Z_]{1,32}$") then . else "INVALID" end) else null end;
+    ($c | resolve($f; $now; $win)) as $s
+    | ($c | if type == "object" then (.state | st) else null end) as $cs
+    | ($c | if type == "object" then (.status | st) else null end) as $cst
+    | {cycle: $cycle, derived_at: $ts, stale_hours: ($win / 3600), file_authoritative: ($fa == 1),
+       state: $s, cache_state: $cs, cache_status: $cst,
+       cache: (if $cache_ok == 0 then "unparseable" elif $c == null then "missing" else "present" end),
+       drift: ($c != null and ($cs != $s or ($cst != null and $cst != $s))),
+       notes: ([
+         (if $cs != null and $cst != null and $cs != $cst then "cache .state \($cs) and .status \($cst) disagree" else empty end),
+         (if $s == "JACKED_OUT" and ($f.all_complete | not) then "JACKED_OUT is terminal: files show incomplete sprints; the cache is kept" else empty end),
+         (if $s == "COMPLETE" and ($f.all_complete | not) then "COMPLETE kept: no new incomplete sprint in the ledger" else empty end),
+         ($f.sprints[] | select(.stale_marker) | "sprint-\(.global_id): COMPLETED marker names another sprint (stale_marker, not counted)"),
+         ($f.sprints[] | select(.state == "awaiting_marker") | "sprint-\(.global_id): review and audit APPROVED, no COMPLETED marker")
+       ]),
+       sprints: $f.sprints,
+       active_sprint: (if $ag == "" then null else "sprint-\($ag)" end),
+       breaker: {state: $b.state, cycle_count: $b.triggers.cycle_count.current, same_issue: $b.triggers.same_issue.count,
+                 no_progress: $b.triggers.no_progress.count, recomputed: {cycle_count: $rc.cycle, same_issue: $rc.same, no_progress: $rc.np}},
+       derivation: {source: "files", stale_markers: $f.stale_markers, legacy_feedback: $f.legacy_feedback},
+       written: false}')
+
+  if (( write )); then
+    local why=""
+    if (( fa == 0 )); then why="run_mode.file_authoritative: false — report-only"
+    elif [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then why="no run state at $file — nothing to rewrite"
+    elif (( cache_ok == 0 )); then why="$file unparseable — kept for inspection, not rewritten"
+    fi
+    if [[ -z "$why" ]]; then
+      atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson rc "$rc" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"' merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts)' || return 3

+      facts=$(jq -c --argjson b "$merged" '.breaker_open = ($b.state == "OPEN")' <<<"$facts")

+        | .state = $s | .status = $s | .derived_at = $ts
+        | .derivation = {source: "files", stale_markers: $f.stale_markers, legacy_feedback: $f.legacy_feedback, sprint_ids: $f.sprint_ids}
+        | .schema_version = (.schema_version // 2)' || return 3
+      report=$(jq -c --slurpfile c "$file" --argjson b "$merged" '.written = true | .state = $c[0].state | .breaker.state = $b.state' <<<"$report")
+    else
+      report=$(jq -c --arg w "$why" '.notes += [$w]' <<<"$report")
+    fi
+  fi
+
+  if (( json )); then
+    jq . <<<"$report"
+  else
+    jq -r '"derive: files say \(.state), cache said \(.cache_state // "nothing") (\(if .drift then "drift" else "in sync" end))"
+           + (if .written then " — caches rewritten" else "" end), (.notes[] | "  note: " + .)' <<<"$report"
+  fi
+  return 0
+}

+cmd_record_round() {
+  [[ -n "$gate" && -n "$file" ]] || usage
+  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: record-round: no feedback file at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
+  local p th ts now out trip
+  p=$(fb_parse "$file" "$gate")
+  if [[ "$(jq -r '.approved' <<<"$p")" == true ]]; then
+    echo "recorded: $gate APPROVED — breaker counters unchanged"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
+              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \
+              --argjson c "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.max_cycles' 20 10000)" \
+              --argjson h "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.timeout_hours' 8 8760)" \
+              '{same: $s, np: $n, cycles: $c, hours: $h}')
+  ts=$(now_iso); now=$(date +%s)
+  atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson p "$p" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$ts" --argjson now "$now" \
+      --arg gate "$gate" --arg sprint "$sprint" "$JQ_DEFS"'
+    (if type == "object" and (.triggers | type) == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
+    | ($p.counts | tojson) as $c
+    | (if $p.hash != "none" and $p.hash == (.triggers.same_issue.last_hash // null)
+       then .triggers.same_issue.count = ((.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) + 1)
+       else .triggers.same_issue.count = 1 | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $p.hash end)
+    | (if (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts // null) != null and .triggers.no_progress.last_counts == $c
+       then .triggers.no_progress.count = ((.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) + 1)
+       else .triggers.no_progress.count = 0 end)
+    | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $c
+    | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ((.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) + 1)
+    | (.triggers.timeout.started // null | epoch) as $start
+    | ( if .triggers.same_issue.count >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
+          then ["same_issue", "same issue hash \($p.hash[0:8]) seen \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times in a row"]
+        elif .triggers.no_progress.count >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
+          then ["no_progress", "finding counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds"]
+        elif .triggers.cycle_count.current >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
+          then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds reached the limit \(.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)"]
+        elif $start != null and ($now - $start) >= ((.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) * 3600)
+          then ["timeout", "run older than \(.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) hours"]
+        elif (.state // "CLOSED") == "OPEN" then ["open", "breaker already OPEN"]
+        else null end ) as $trip
+    | .last_round = {gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end), verdict: $p.verdict, hash: $p.hash, ts: $ts}
+    | if $trip != null and $trip[0] != "open" and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
+      then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end)}])
+      elif $trip != null then .state = "OPEN"
+      else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end
+    | .last_trip = $trip' || return 3
+  trip=$(jq -r '.last_trip // empty | if type == "array" then "\(.[0]): \(.[1])" else empty end' "$breaker")
+  out=$(jq -r '"recorded: \(.last_round.gate) \(.last_round.verdict // "no verdict") — cycle \(.triggers.cycle_count.current)/\(.triggers.cycle_count.limit), same_issue \(.triggers.same_issue.count)/\(.triggers.same_issue.threshold), no_progress \(.triggers.no_progress.count)/\(.triggers.no_progress.threshold)"' "$breaker")
+  echo "$out"
+  if [[ -n "$trip" ]]; then
+    atomic_update "$state_file" --arg ts "$ts" '.state = "HALTED"' || return 3
+    echo "TRIPPED: $trip"
+    return 10
+  fi
+  return 0
+}
+
+cmd_mark() {
+  [[ -n "$skill" && -n "$sprint" ]] || usage
+  mkdir -p "$run_dir"
+  atomic_update "$run_dir/implement-active.json" --arg k "$skill" --arg s "$sprint" --arg ts "$(now_iso)" \
+    '{skill: $k, sprint: $s, started_at: $ts}' || return 3

+    local err drc=0
+    err=$( { write=1; json=0; cmd_derive >/dev/null; } 2>&1 ) || drc=$?
+    if (( drc != 0 && drc != 4 )); then printf '%s\n' "$err" >&2; fi
+  fi
+  echo "marked: $skill $sprint ($run_dir/implement-active.json)"
+}
+

-  write) cmd_write ;;
-  read)  cmd_read ;;

+  read)   cmd_read ;;
