+# SINCE touching a path outside the state/generated set, or nothing
+impl_commit() {
+  git -C "$root" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  git -C "$root" log --no-merges -n 1 --format='%H %ct' ${1:+"--since=$1"} -- . \
+    ':(exclude,glob)grimoires/**' ':(exclude,glob).run/**' ':(exclude,glob)**/REPO-MAP.md' \
+    ':(exclude,glob)**/checksums.json' ':(exclude,glob)**/CHANGELOG.md' 2>/dev/null || true
+}
+
+# The ordered rounds of one sprint directory: every -rN file, then the current
+# file unless it is byte-identical to the highest -rN of its gate
+rounds_of() {
+  local dir="$1" g base f n top topn cur
+  for g in review audit; do
+    if [[ "$g" == review ]]; then base=engineer-feedback; else base=auditor-sprint-feedback; fi
+    top=""; topn=-1
+    for f in "$dir/$base"-r*.md; do
+      [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
+      n=${f##*-r}; n=${n%.md}
+      [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]{1,6}$ ]] || continue
+      fb_parse "$f" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" --argjson n "$((10#$n))" '. + {gate: $g, round: $n}'
+      if (( 10#$n > topn )); then topn=$((10#$n)); top="$f"; fi
+    done
+    cur="$dir/$base.md"
+    if [[ -f "$cur" ]] && ! { [[ -n "$top" ]] && cmp -s "$cur" "$top"; }; then
+      fb_parse "$cur" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" '. + {gate: $g, round: 999999}'
+    fi
+  done
+}
+
+# Shared jq definitions: time, the breaker recompute and the run-state resolution
+JQ_DEFS='
+def epoch: if type == "string" then (sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch null) else null end;
+def fresh($now; $win): epoch as $t | $t != null and ($now - $t) <= $win and ($t - $now) <= 300;
+def recompute($rounds; $reset):
+  ($rounds
+   | map(select($reset == null or ((.ts // "") > $reset)))
+   | sort_by([(.ts // ""), .round, (if .gate == "review" then 0 else 1 end)])
+   | map(select(.approved | not))) as $nr
+  | reduce $nr[] as $r ({cycle: 0, same: 0, hash: null, np: 0, lc: null};
+      .cycle += 1
+      | (if $r.hash != "none" and $r.hash == .hash then .same += 1 else .same = 1 | .hash = $r.hash end)
+      | ($r.counts | tojson) as $c
+      | (if .lc != null and .lc == $c then .np += 1 else .np = 0 end)
+      | .lc = $c);
+def skeleton($th; $ts):
+  {state: "CLOSED",
+   triggers: {same_issue: {count: 0, threshold: $th.same, last_hash: null},
+              no_progress: {count: 0, threshold: $th.np},
+              cycle_count: {current: 0, limit: $th.cycles},
+              timeout: {started: $ts, limit_hours: $th.hours}},
+   history: []};
+def merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts):
+  (if type == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
+  | .triggers = (.triggers // {})
+  | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ([(.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0), $rc.cycle] | max)
+  | (if $rc.same > (.triggers.same_issue.count // 0)
+     then .triggers.same_issue.count = $rc.same | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $rc.hash else . end)
+  | (if $rc.np > (.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) or (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts == null and $rc.lc != null)
+     then .triggers.no_progress.count = ([(.triggers.no_progress.count // 0), $rc.np] | max)
+          | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $rc.lc else . end)
+  | ( if (.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
+        then ["same_issue", "same issue hash repeated \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times (derived from the feedback history)"]
+      elif (.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
+        then ["no_progress", "counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds (derived from the feedback history)"]
+      elif (.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
+        then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds (derived from the feedback history)"]
+      else null end ) as $trip
+  | if $trip != null and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
+    then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], source: "derive"}])
+    else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end;
+def known_ids: (.derivation.sprint_ids // null) // ((.sprints.list // []) | map(.id? // empty));
+def resolve($f; $now; $win):
+  . as $c
+  | (if ($c | type) == "object" then $c else {} end) as $c
+  | ($c.state // $c.status // "") as $cs
+  | ($c | known_ids) as $known
+  | ([$f.sprints[] | select(.state != "complete")
+      | "sprint-\(.global_id)" as $g | .local_label as $l
+      | select(($known | index($g)) == null and ($l == "" or ($known | index($l)) == null))] | length > 0) as $new
+  | ((($c.completion // {}) | .merged_sha? // "") | type == "string" and length > 0) as $merged
+  | if ($c.state // "") == "JACKED_OUT" or ($c.status // "") == "JACKED_OUT" or $merged then "JACKED_OUT"
+    elif $f.breaker_open or $cs == "HALTED" then "HALTED"
+    elif $f.all_complete then "COMPLETE"
+    elif $cs == "COMPLETE" and ($new | not) then "COMPLETE"
+    elif ($c.timestamps.last_activity? // null) | fresh($now; $win) then "RUNNING"
+    else "INTERRUPTED" end;
+'
+
+cmd_derive() {
+  local ledger="$root/grimoires/loa/ledger.json" a2a="$root/grimoires/loa/a2a" active rows
+  if [[ ! -f "$ledger" ]] || ! jq -e 'type == "object"' "$ledger" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "run-checkpoint: derive: no readable ledger at $ledger — callers keep the cache" >&2; return 4
+  fi
+  active=$(jq -r '.active_cycle // empty | strings' "$ledger")
+  if [[ -z "$active" ]] || ! jq -e --arg c "$active" 'any(.cycles[]?; .id == $c)' "$ledger" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "run-checkpoint: derive: the ledger has no active cycle — callers keep the cache" >&2; return 4
+  fi
+  local win now now_ts fa=1 th
+  win=$(( $(cfg_int '.run_mode.stale_hours' 12 8760) * 3600 ))
+  [[ "$(cfg '.run_mode.file_authoritative')" == false ]] && fa=0
+  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
+              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \
+              --argjson c "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.max_cycles' 20 10000)" \
+              --argjson h "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.timeout_hours' 8 8760)" \
+              '{same: $s, np: $n, cycles: $c, hours: $h}')
+  now=$(date +%s); now_ts=$(now_iso)
+
+  # Per-sprint facts
+  local sprints="[]" gid label lstatus since dir rv au mex msid ic sj
+  rows=$(jq -r --arg c "$active" '
+    (.cycles[] | select(.id == $c)) as $cy
+    | ($cy.sprints // [])[]
+    | select((.global_id | type) == "number")
+    | [(.global_id | tostring), ((.local_label // "") | tostring), ((.status // "") | tostring),
+       ([.started, .created, $cy.created] | map(select(type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-")))
+        | if length == 0 then "" else ([.[0], ($cy.created // "")] | max) end)]
+    | map(if . == "" then "-" else . end)
+    | @tsv' "$ledger")
+  # "-" stands for an empty field: IFS whitespace (tab) would collapse two adjacent separators
+  while IFS=$'\t' read -r gid label lstatus since; do
+    [[ "$gid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
+    [[ "$label" == - ]] && label=""
+    [[ "$since" == - ]] && since=""
+    [[ "$label" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$ ]] || label=""
+    [[ "$lstatus" =~ ^[a-z_]{1,32}$ ]] || lstatus="unknown"
+    [[ "$since" =~ ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$ ]] || since=""
+    dir="$a2a/sprint-$gid"
+    rv=$(fb_parse "$dir/engineer-feedback.md" review)
+    au=$(fb_parse "$dir/auditor-sprint-feedback.md" audit)
+    mex=false; msid=""
+    if [[ -f "$dir/COMPLETED" ]]; then
+      mex=true
+      msid=$(sed -n 's/^sprint:[[:space:]]*\([A-Za-z0-9._-]*\).*/\1/p' "$dir/COMPLETED" | head -n 1) || msid=""
+    fi
+    ic=$(impl_commit "$since")
+    sj=$(jq -nc --argjson gid "$gid" --arg label "$label" --arg status "$lstatus" --argjson rv "$rv" --argjson au "$au" \
+              --argjson mex "$mex" --arg msid "$msid" --arg ic "$ic" '
+      def mine: type == "string" and length > 0 and (. == "sprint-\($gid)" or ($label != "" and . == $label));
+      ($rv.approved == true and ($rv.sprint_id | mine)) as $R
+      | ($au.approved == true and ($au.sprint_id | mine)) as $A
+      | ([$rv.sprint_id, $au.sprint_id, (if $msid == "" then null else $msid end)] | map(select(type == "string" and length > 0))) as $ids
+      | ($mex and any($ids[]; mine | not)) as $stale
+      | ($mex and ($stale | not) and (($rv.sprint_id | mine) or ($au.sprint_id | mine))) as $M
+      | ($ic | split(" ")) as $c
+      | ([$rv.ts, $au.ts] | map(select(. != null)) | max) as $vts
+      | def verdict($x): if $x.exists then {verdict: $x.verdict, sprint_id: $x.sprint_id, consistent: ($x.exit_code == 0), file: $x.file} else null end;
+      {global_id: $gid, local_label: $label, status: $status,
+       completed_marker: $M, marker_present: $mex, stale_marker: $stale,
+       review: verdict($rv), audit: verdict($au),
+       impl_commit: (if ($c | length) == 2 then $c[0] else null end),
+       commit_after_verdict: (if ($c | length) == 2 and $vts != null
+                              then (($c[1] | tonumber) > ($vts | sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch 0)) else null end),
+       legacy_feedback: ([$rv, $au] | map(select(.exists and (.trailer | not)) | .file)),
+       state: (if $M and $R and $A and $status == "completed" then "complete"
+               elif ($M | not) and $R and $A then "awaiting_marker" else "in_progress" end)}')
+    sprints=$(jq -c --argjson s "$sj" '. + [$s]' <<<"$sprints")
+  done <<<"$rows"
+
+  # Breaker recompute over the active sprint's ordered rounds
+  local active_gid rounds cache="null" cache_ok=1 bcache="null" reset rc merged
+  active_gid=$(jq -r 'if length == 0 then "" else ((map(select(.state != "complete")) | .[0]) // .[-1]) | .global_id | tostring end' <<<"$sprints")
+  rounds="[]"
+  if [[ -n "$active_gid" && -d "$a2a/sprint-$active_gid" ]]; then
+    rounds=$(rounds_of "$a2a/sprint-$active_gid" | jq -sc '.')
+  fi
+  if [[ -f "$file" ]]; then
+    if cache=$(jq -c . "$file" 2>/dev/null) && [[ -n "$cache" ]]; then :; else cache="null"; cache_ok=0; fi
+  fi
+  if [[ -f "$breaker" ]]; then bcache=$(jq -c 'if type == "object" then . else null end' "$breaker" 2>/dev/null) || bcache="null"; [[ -n "$bcache" ]] || bcache="null"; fi
+  reset=$(jq -c '.reset_at? // null | if type == "string" then . else null end' <<<"$bcache")
+  rc=$(jq -nc --argjson r "$rounds" --argjson z "$reset" "$JQ_DEFS"' recompute($r; $z)')
+  merged=$(jq -c --argjson rc "$rc" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"' merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts)' <<<"$bcache")
+
+  local facts report
+  facts=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$sprints" --argjson b "$merged" '
+    {sprints: $s,
+     all_complete: (($s | length) > 0 and all($s[]; .state == "complete")),
+     breaker_open: ($b.state == "OPEN"),
+     stale_markers: [$s[] | select(.stale_marker) | "sprint-\(.global_id)"],
+     legacy_feedback: [$s[] | .legacy_feedback[]],
+     sprint_ids: [$s[] | "sprint-\(.global_id)"]}')
+  report=$(jq -nc --argjson f "$facts" --argjson c "$cache" --argjson b "$merged" --argjson rc "$rc" \
+                  --argjson now "$now" --argjson win "$win" --arg ts "$now_ts" --arg cycle "$active" \
+                  --argjson fa "$fa" --argjson cache_ok "$cache_ok" --arg ag "$active_gid" "$JQ_DEFS"'
+    def st: if type == "string" then (if test("^[A-Z_]{1,32}$") then . else "INVALID" end) else null end;
+    ($c | resolve($f; $now; $win)) as $s
+    | ($c | if type == "object" then (.state | st) else null end) as $cs
+    | ($c | if type == "object" then (.status | st) else null end) as $cst
+    | {cycle: $cycle, derived_at: $ts, stale_hours: ($win / 3600), file_authoritative: ($fa == 1),
+       state: $s, cache_state: $cs, cache_status: $cst,
+       cache: (if $cache_ok == 0 then "unparseable" elif $c == null then "missing" else "present" end),
+       drift: ($c != null and ($cs != $s or ($cst != null and $cst != $s))),
+       notes: ([
+         (if $cs != null and $cst != null and $cs != $cst then "cache .state \($cs) and .status \($cst) disagree" else empty end),
+         (if $s == "JACKED_OUT" and ($f.all_complete | not) then "JACKED_OUT is terminal: files show incomplete sprints; the cache is kept" else empty end),
+         (if $s == "COMPLETE" and ($f.all_complete | not) then "COMPLETE kept: no new incomplete sprint in the ledger" else empty end),
+         ($f.sprints[] | select(.stale_marker) | "sprint-\(.global_id): COMPLETED marker names another sprint (stale_marker, not counted)"),
+         ($f.sprints[] | select(.state == "awaiting_marker") | "sprint-\(.global_id): review and audit APPROVED, no COMPLETED marker")
+       ]),
+       sprints: $f.sprints,
+       active_sprint: (if $ag == "" then null else "sprint-\($ag)" end),
+       breaker: {state: $b.state, cycle_count: $b.triggers.cycle_count.current, same_issue: $b.triggers.same_issue.count,
+                 no_progress: $b.triggers.no_progress.count, recomputed: {cycle_count: $rc.cycle, same_issue: $rc.same, no_progress: $rc.np}},
+       derivation: {source: "files", stale_markers: $f.stale_markers, legacy_feedback: $f.legacy_feedback},
+       written: false}')
+
+  if (( write )); then
+    local why=""
+    if (( fa == 0 )); then why="run_mode.file_authoritative: false — report-only"
+    elif [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then why="no run state at $file — nothing to rewrite"
+    elif (( cache_ok == 0 )); then why="$file unparseable — kept for inspection, not rewritten"
+    fi
+    if [[ -z "$why" ]]; then
+      atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson rc "$rc" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"' merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts)' || return 3
+      merged=$(jq -c . "$breaker")
+      facts=$(jq -c --argjson b "$merged" '.breaker_open = ($b.state == "OPEN")' <<<"$facts")
+      atomic_update "$file" --argjson f "$facts" --argjson now "$now" --argjson win "$win" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"'
+        resolve($f; $now; $win) as $s
+        | .state = $s | .status = $s | .derived_at = $ts
+        | .derivation = {source: "files", stale_markers: $f.stale_markers, legacy_feedback: $f.legacy_feedback, sprint_ids: $f.sprint_ids}
+        | .schema_version = (.schema_version // 2)' || return 3
+      report=$(jq -c --slurpfile c "$file" --argjson b "$merged" '.written = true | .state = $c[0].state | .breaker.state = $b.state' <<<"$report")
+    else
+      report=$(jq -c --arg w "$why" '.notes += [$w]' <<<"$report")
+    fi
+  fi
+
+  if (( json )); then
+    jq . <<<"$report"
+  else
+    jq -r '"derive: files say \(.state), cache said \(.cache_state // "nothing") (\(if .drift then "drift" else "in sync" end))"
+           + (if .written then " — caches rewritten" else "" end), (.notes[] | "  note: " + .)' <<<"$report"
+  fi
+  return 0
+}

+cmd_record_round() {
+  [[ -n "$gate" && -n "$file" ]] || usage
+  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: record-round: no feedback file at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
+  local p th ts now out trip
+  p=$(fb_parse "$file" "$gate")
+  if [[ "$(jq -r '.approved' <<<"$p")" == true ]]; then
+    echo "recorded: $gate APPROVED — breaker counters unchanged"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
+              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \
+              --argjson c "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.max_cycles' 20 10000)" \
+              --argjson h "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.timeout_hours' 8 8760)" \
+              '{same: $s, np: $n, cycles: $c, hours: $h}')
+  ts=$(now_iso); now=$(date +%s)
+  atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson p "$p" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$ts" --argjson now "$now" \
+      --arg gate "$gate" --arg sprint "$sprint" "$JQ_DEFS"'
+    (if type == "object" and (.triggers | type) == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
+    | ($p.counts | tojson) as $c
+    | (if $p.hash != "none" and $p.hash == (.triggers.same_issue.last_hash // null)
+       then .triggers.same_issue.count = ((.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) + 1)
+       else .triggers.same_issue.count = 1 | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $p.hash end)
+    | (if (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts // null) != null and .triggers.no_progress.last_counts == $c
+       then .triggers.no_progress.count = ((.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) + 1)
+       else .triggers.no_progress.count = 0 end)
+    | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $c
+    | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ((.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) + 1)
+    | (.triggers.timeout.started // null | epoch) as $start
+    | ( if .triggers.same_issue.count >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
+          then ["same_issue", "same issue hash \($p.hash[0:8]) seen \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times in a row"]
+        elif .triggers.no_progress.count >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
+          then ["no_progress", "finding counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds"]
+        elif .triggers.cycle_count.current >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
+          then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds reached the limit \(.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)"]
+        elif $start != null and ($now - $start) >= ((.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) * 3600)
+          then ["timeout", "run older than \(.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) hours"]
+        elif (.state // "CLOSED") == "OPEN" then ["open", "breaker already OPEN"]
+        else null end ) as $trip
+    | .last_round = {gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end), verdict: $p.verdict, hash: $p.hash, ts: $ts}
+    | if $trip != null and $trip[0] != "open" and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
+      then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end)}])
+      elif $trip != null then .state = "OPEN"
+      else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end
+    | .last_trip = $trip' || return 3
+  trip=$(jq -r '.last_trip // empty | if type == "array" then "\(.[0]): \(.[1])" else empty end' "$breaker")
+  out=$(jq -r '"recorded: \(.last_round.gate) \(.last_round.verdict // "no verdict") — cycle \(.triggers.cycle_count.current)/\(.triggers.cycle_count.limit), same_issue \(.triggers.same_issue.count)/\(.triggers.same_issue.threshold), no_progress \(.triggers.no_progress.count)/\(.triggers.no_progress.threshold)"' "$breaker")
+  echo "$out"
+  if [[ -n "$trip" ]]; then
+    atomic_update "$state_file" --arg ts "$ts" '.state = "HALTED"' || return 3
+    echo "TRIPPED: $trip"
+    return 10
+  fi
+  return 0
+}
+
+cmd_mark() {

+#!/usr/bin/env bash

+# profile-lib.sh (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, sprint-256 Task 2.7).

+# own `yq '.<key> // <default>'`: a direct read skips the profile, and yq's
+# `//` reads an explicit `false` as absent. The check flags a line that names a
+# profile key in yq-path form (a leading dot: `.guardrails.input.enabled`)
+# under .claude/ (scripts, hooks, skills, data) and tools/, except
+# profile-lib.sh itself. Prose that names a key without the dot
+# (`guardrails.input.enabled: false`) is not a read and is not flagged.
+#
+# Misses: a key assembled at runtime (".guardrails.input.${x}.enabled") and a
+# reader in a language that indexes the config as nested keys.
+#
+# Usage: tools/check-knob-readers.sh [--root DIR]
+# Exit:  0 clean · 1 direct read found (each printed as path:line) · 2 usage
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+ROOT="."
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    -h|--help) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit:/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;

+  esac
+done

+[[ -f "$PROFILES" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: $PROFILES not found" >&2; exit 2; }

+
+keys=$(yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort -u)
+[[ -n "$keys" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no profile keys in $PROFILES" >&2; exit 2; }
+# Alternation of the dot-escaped keys; each must be preceded by a dot that is
+# not itself part of an identifier (start of line, quote, space, paren, ...).
+alt=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | sed 's/\./\\./g' | paste -sd'|' -)
+pattern="(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])\\.(${alt})([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)"
+

+  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?\.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib\.sh:' \

== implement-gate
not ok 1 IG-1 a lead-session payload carrying tool_input.active_skill records active_skill_seen_at and its source

not ok 3 IG-3 a teammate role or a subagent payload writes nothing
not ok 4 IG-4 the corpus' records_evidence column holds for every fixture
not ok 5 IG-5 a forged active_skill Write payload does not flip the gate, whatever .run/ claims
not ok 6 IG-6 without the opt-in the gate stays heuristic: every corpus fixture gets its heuristic decision
not ok 7 IG-7 with implement_gate.mode: authoritative the branch passes the payload corpus
not ok 8 IG-8 the authoritative branch falls back to the heuristic on a payload without active_skill (RUNNING allows, absent asks)
== profile-lib
not ok 5 PL-5 precedence: explicit key beats the profile, the profile beats the fallback
not ok 8 PL-8 the cache is written once and rebuilt when the config or profiles.yaml changes
not ok 12 PL-12 a profiles.yaml key that names a floor key is ignored with a WARN
not ok 14 PL-14 the /loa Profile line prints the profile and the explicit overrides

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/karpathy-surgical-diff.bats — cycle-129 sprint-256 Task 2.3
# (AC-2.3; PRD AC-4.3; SDD D-4.3, D-4.2a; DEC-0141)
#
# The surgical-diff hook keys its running total on the checkpoint task
# (`run-checkpoint.sh read --json`), else the sprint, else the session id;
# keeps one sanitised file per task under the state directory (at most 20);
# deletes the legacy session-long file; writes the summary the review's
# SURGICAL axis reads; and is silent when the knob is off. A fixture
# checkpoint (LOA_RUN_DIR) and a fake `br` on PATH stand in for a live run.
# =============================================================================

bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0

setup() {
    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    HOOK="$R/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh"
    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not available"
    command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not available"
    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
    export LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$T/config.yaml"
    export KARPATHY_STATE_DIR="$T/state"
    export KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE="$T/summary.json"
    export KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE="$T/karpathy-task-state.jsonl"
    export KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR="$T/trajectory"
    export LOA_RUN_DIR="$T/run"
    unset LOA_SESSION_ID LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE
    mkdir -p "$T/run" "$T/bin"
    printf 'karpathy_principles:\n  surgical_diff_warning: true\n  diff_lines_per_task: 5\n' > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE"
    # Fake beads: every bead reports closed unless BR_STATUS says otherwise.
    printf '%s\n' '#!/usr/bin/env bash' 'printf "{\"status\":\"%s\"}\n" "${BR_STATUS:-closed}"' > "$T/bin/br"
    chmod +x "$T/bin/br"
    export PATH="$T/bin:$PATH"
}

# checkpoint <sprint> [task] — a schema-2 run state with that checkpoint
checkpoint() {
    jq -n --arg s "$1" --arg t "${2:-}" \
        '{schema_version: 2, state: "RUNNING",
          checkpoint: {sprint: $s, task: (if $t == "" then null else $t end), phase: "IMPLEMENT", ts: "2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"}}' \
        > "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json"
}

# write_lines <n> [session_id] — one Write payload adding n lines
write_lines() {
    local n="$1" sid="${2:-sess-1}" content
    content=$(seq 1 "$n" | paste -sd'\n' -)
    jq -nc --arg c "$content" --arg s "$sid" \
        '{tool_name: "Write", session_id: $s, tool_input: {file_path: "/repo/src/x.sh", content: $c}}' \
        | bash "$HOOK"
}

@test "KS-1 the counter resets when the checkpoint task changes" {
    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-aaa
    write_lines 3
    write_lines 2
    [ "$(jq -r '.task' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "bd-aaa" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.lines' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "5" ]
    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-bbb

head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:538 — `_bdb_hd_segword` strips wrappers, quotes, parens and assignments, but not shell reserved words (`if`, `then`, `do`, `else`, `while`, `until`). Nothing re-checks the body when a later line runs the written file without naming its basename literally. Reproduced against the hook: `cat > d/x <<'EOF'` + `if true; then rm -rf ~; fi` + `EOF` + `bash d/*` exits 0 (base exits 2). So does `cat > Makefile <<'EOF'` with the same recipe followed by `make clean` (base exits 2). Same-command execution regresses from blocked to allowed. The documented gap only covers a LATER command.
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:732 — The knob comment says "turning it off only tightens", and the same claim appears at head/.loa.config.yaml.example:1243 and in hooks-reference. It is false. With `heredoc_classifier: false` the old #1245 scrub drops the whole body of `cat > run.sh <<'EOF'` / `rm -rf ~` / `EOF` and the command is allowed (exit 0). With the classifier on, the `.sh` target makes it interpreter-class and the command is blocked (exit 2). Operators told this is a safe rollback key would loosen the fence. Fix the wording or make the knob-off path keep the exec-destination checks.
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:280 — The breaker recompute counts every round with `approved == false`, and that includes legacy trailerless feedback, which the header says yields "no verdict". Trailerless files with no Findings/Issues heading all hash to md5("") and all have counts `null`, so same_issue and no_progress climb. Reproduced: a RUNNING cache, then a sprint dir holding engineer-feedback-r1/-r2/engineer-feedback.md ("All good") and auditor-sprint-feedback.md ("APPROVED") in legacy form, then `derive --write`. The breaker opens (same_issue 4) and sprint-plan-state.json is rewritten to HALTED. Every `checkpoint write` and `mark` runs this, so approved legacy history halts a live run. Legacy rounds should be excluded from the recompute.
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:295 — `merge_breaker` uses the skeleton only when the input is not an object. But `atomic_update` (line 154) feeds `{}` for a missing breaker file, so `derive --write` creates circuit-breaker.json with no thresholds, no `cycle_count.limit` and no `timeout.started`. `record-round` then sees `.triggers` as an object, never applies its skeleton either, and the timeout trigger can never fire. The record-round header promises "a missing breaker file is created from the schema defaults", but this path does not do that.
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378 — `derive` does not run on jq 1.6, which is still the distro jq on Ubuntu 22.04 and Debian 11, with no minimum version stated. First, `--arg label` / `$label` is a keyword binding error on jq 1.6 ("syntax error, unexpected label"), so every derive fails. Second, at lines 223/226 `jq -e 'type == "object"' <<<""` exits 0 on 1.6, so the fallbacks never fire for an empty verdict-derive result or a trailerless file, and `--argjson p ''` aborts under `set -e`. Rename the variable and guard against empty input.
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:197 — The switch to `set -euo pipefail` (line 78) breaks `read`'s contract ("Exit 0 always when F exists"). A malformed `.checkpoint` (e.g. a string) makes `jq '.checkpoint.sprint'` fail, and the script exits 5. Base returned `{"checkpoint":null,"reason":"malformed checkpoint"}` with exit 0. The karpathy hook and resume paths depend on `read` never failing.
head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:131 — The per-task key comes from `run-checkpoint.sh read --json`. But `read` drops any task checkpoint whose bead is not confirmed closed in beads, and it always drops it when `br` is unavailable. While a task is being implemented its bead is open, so the key falls back to the sprint (or to the last closed task, so the new task's lines land in the previous task's file). The "per task" total and the `.run/karpathy-surgical/<bead>.jsonl` file the SURGICAL review axis reads are therefore mis-keyed. Each Write also now forks run-checkpoint plus `br show`.
head/tests/unit/karpathy-surgical-diff.bats:32 — The fake `br` reports every bead `closed` by default. That hides the defect above: in a real run the current task's bead is open and the checkpoint task is discarded. Add a case with an open current bead.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:77 — The cache id comes from `stat -Lc … cfg profiles floor || stat -Lf …`. When any one of the three files is missing (no floor.yaml or profiles.yaml in a partial or older install, or no config), GNU stat exits 1 and the `||` runs `stat -Lf`, which on GNU means file-system status. The id then holds no mtime or size. Reproduced with floor.yaml absent: after editing `guardrails.input.enabled` from true to false in .loa.config.yaml, `knob` kept returning the cached `true` until the cache was deleted. Keep the first stat's output whatever its exit status, or stat each existing file separately.
head/.claude/data/skill-includes/retrospective_postlude.md:1 — `profile-lib.sh knob invisible_retrospective.enabled` is called with no fallback, while resources/retrospective-postlude.md documents `… knob invisible_retrospective.enabled true`. When jq or yq is unavailable, loa_knob prints the empty fallback and the retrospective is silently skipped, which differs from the documented default. Pass `true` here as the resource file does.
head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:193 — The warning still says "Session diff total" although the total is now per task (or per sprint). The message misstates what was counted.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

My review is in `/workspace/review.md`. It has 11 findings, and the verdict is **CHANGES_REQUIRED**. Most of the serious ones I reproduced by running the changed scripts on small test setups in `/tmp`; nothing under `pr/` was changed.

**Blocking issues**
- **The destructive-command check now misses some commands.** When the new heredoc classifier decides a heredoc's text won't be executed, it skips lines that start with a shell keyword like `then` or `do`. If the same command then runs that text without naming the file (`bash d/*`, `make clean`), a `rm -rf ~` gets through. The hook now allows both of those examples; before the change it blocked them.
- **The "rollback" setting is not safe.** The comments say setting `heredoc_classifier: false` "only tightens". It actually loosens: `cat > run.sh <<'EOF'` followed by `rm -rf ~` is blocked with the classifier on and allowed with it off.
- **Old review files halt a running run.** `run-checkpoint.sh derive` counts review files without the new verdict trailer as failed rounds, even when they say approved, and they all look like the same issue. In my test, four such files opened the circuit breaker and rewrote a running run's state to HALTED. This step runs on every checkpoint write and every `mark`.
- **Breaker file built without limits.** When the breaker file is missing, `derive --write` creates it without thresholds, a cycle limit or a timeout start time. After that, the timeout trigger can never fire.
- **Doesn't work on jq 1.6** (the default on Ubuntu 22.04). `derive` uses `$label` as a variable name, which jq 1.6 rejects, so derive always fails there. Its empty-input checks also pass on jq 1.6 when they should fail.
- **`read` can now crash.** Switching `run-checkpoint.sh` to `set -e` means a malformed checkpoint makes `read` exit 5. It used to report "malformed checkpoint" and exit 0, which its documentation still promises.
- **The per-task line counter is mis-keyed.** The diff-size hook takes the task from `run-checkpoint.sh read`, which throws away any checkpoint whose task isn't closed yet. The task being worked on is always open, so lines go to the sprint or to the previous task. The test hides this because its fake `br` reports every task as closed.
- **Stale cached settings.** If one of the three profile input files is missing (I tested with `floor.yaml` missing), the profile cache is never invalidated. In my test, a setting I changed from true to false in `.loa.config.yaml` kept reading `true` until I deleted the cache.

**Minor**
- The retrospective include calls the profile lookup with no default.
- The diff-size warning still says "Session diff total" although it now counts per task.

The new implement-gate modes worked as described in a quick check. Deny mode refused the write, the marker, run state and override each allowed it, and ask was the fallback when the run position was unknown.

I couldn't run the PR's bats suites meaningfully. Only the touched files are in `pr/`, so most tests fail for missing dependencies. Two test files are also unreadable because a test secret was replaced with "REDACTED" when the PR was frozen, which looks like a packaging artifact, not a defect in the change.
